articles.title: United Airlines outage: What you're entitled to when flights are delayed or canceled
articles.summary: Flight delays and cancellations can put a damper on your holiday plans, but many airlines offer travelers some form of compensation.
articles.body:

United Airlines said it has resolved a system outage on Monday afternoon, a disruption that affected departing flights just days after a nationwide ground stop disrupted air travel across the U.S.

The Chicago-based airline said travelers should check their flight status at united.com . The outage came as U.S. airlines and travelers were still recovering from Friday's hours-long ground stop , which left tens of thousands of flights delayed or canceled.

The disruption hit a week before the Thanksgiving travel rush, one of the busiest times of year to travel. Despite high prices from rising jet fuel costs , nearly 29 million passengers are expected to fly over Thanksgiving weekend, according to Airlines for America , a trade association for U.S. airlines.

Airlines are increasing the number of seats available across the holiday weekend, the organization said, and the days following Thanksgiving — Sunday, Nov. 29 and Monday, Nov. 30 — will be the busiest times to fly.

No matter when you plan to fly this holiday season, though, there's always a risk of travel disruptions derailing your plans. Higher volumes of travelers and potential weather-related delays can always put a strain on airports, which is why now is a great time to brush up on your airline's fine print.

What you're entitled to in the event of a delay or cancellation

Picture this: Your bags are packed, you arrive at the airport, and you're counting down the hours until takeoff. Then you get an alert that your flight has been delayed, or worse, canceled. For travelers, especially during the holiday season, this can feel incredibly disheartening. Even if there's a wrench thrown into your travel plans, it doesn't mean all is lost.

Many airlines offer some compensation in the event of a "controllable" flight cancellation or delay. A controllable cancellation or delay is an event caused by the airline, such as a maintenance issue with your aircraft, a delay due to cabin cleaning or fueling, or a crew-related issue.

In the event of a controllable cancellation or delay, travelers have rights. These may include:

Rebooking on the same airline at no additional cost

Rebooking on a partner airline or a different airline at no additional cost

Meal or meal/cash voucher when a cancellation results in a passenger waiting for three hours or longer for a new flight

Complimentary hotel accommodations for passengers affected by overnight cancellations as well as complimentary ground transportation to and from hotels

A credit or travel voucher when a cancellation results in a passenger waiting three hours or more from the scheduled departure time

Frequent flier miles when a cancellation results in a passenger waiting for three hours or more from the scheduled departure time

"If a flight gets canceled, consumers have a right to get a full refund," said Lorelei Salas, former supervision director for the CFPB and former commissioner for the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection. "Regardless of whatever the reason is for the cancellation, the airlines can offer you rebooking and/or travel credits or vouchers, but you can say no and ask for your full refund. Also, when there are significant delays or changes in the travel itinerary, consumers are also entitled to a full refund. But that means a delay of — or a change in a flight of — at least three hours if it is a domestic flight and three hours if it's an international flight."

Salas said that significant changes aren't just limited to the scheduled departure time; there are other instances when you have the right to request a full refund.

"Significant changes could also include if the airline decides that you are going to depart from a different airport or arrive at a different airport," Salas said. "Or in some cases, if you have a disability and the aircraft that was going to accommodate your disability is no longer available, you may also be able to request a full refund on your ticket."

Each airline has its own policies regarding what it offers in the event of a delay or cancellation, so it's important to read and understand the terms and conditions of your booking as well as any voucher you receive.

If your airline has committed to offering some kind of compensation, it can be held accountable by the Department of Transportation. If any airline doesn't adhere to its terms and conditions, or you have been denied a refund you feel you are entitled to, you have the right to file a complaint with the Department of Transportation.

How your credit card perks can come in handy

Some travel insurance policies can provide you with extra protection if your flight is canceled or delayed, but this isn't necessarily a guarantee, and your policy may not cover every eventuality.

"A lot of people rely on travel insurance, and they think that maybe that's going to give them all the protections they need," Salas said. "It's really important that people pay close attention when they're buying travel insurance — to make sure that there aren't restrictions on terms that are later going to surprise them."

The good news is that some credit cards may help fill the gaps if you don't have travel insurance or your policy doesn't cover a delayed or canceled flight. These perks may include:

Reimbursement for hotel accommodations and meals if your flight is delayed

Reimbursement for the cost of eligible items, such as toiletries and clothing, if an airline or other common carrier causes a delay of six or more hours

Reimbursement for delays or cancellations caused by severe weather

Contact your credit card issuer or review your card's benefits guide to learn more about how your travel insurance perks can keep you covered.

articles.title: Escala 5x2: Fachin prioriza julgamento no STF sobre novas regras | G1
articles.summary: Escala 5x2: Edson Fachin sinaliza pressa para que o STF decida sobre o início das 42 horas semanais antes da mudança prevista para o dia 16 de dezembro.
articles.body:
O presidente do STF , Edson Fachin , indicou a colegas que pretende pautar logo o julgamento da escala 5x2, que foi transferido para o plenário físico do STF na última semana a pedido do ministro Luiz Fux .

O ponto central da discussão é o adiamento ou não das novas regras.

Segundo fontes do STF, o presidente reconhece a urgência do tema e a importância de o plenário da Corte definir o tema antes da entrada em vigor da primeira parte das mudanças, em 16 de dezembro.

Antes do pedido de Fux para que o tema fosse para o plenário físico, já haviam quatro votos pelo não adiamento da entrada em vigor das 42 horas semanais, uma etapa de transição.

Três ministros já haviam acompanhado o relator, Flávio Dino .

O único ponto que pode deixar o julgamento em aberto seria um pedido de vista.

Mesmo assim, há chances de que votos sejam antecipados para formar a maioria e reforçar que não haverá adiamento na entrada em vigor das novas regras.

Julgamento de ações que questionam o fim da escala 6x1 foi transferido para o plenário presencial do STF — Foto: Gustavo Moreno/STF

articles.title: Alemanha se despede da Adidas em último jogo após 77 anos de parceria; Nike assume em 2027  | G1
articles.standfirst: Partida contra a Holanda, nesta segunda-feira (16), marca o fim de uma parceria de 77 anos. A partir de 2027, a Nike assumirá o posto em um contrato de R$ 633 milhões por ano.
articles.summary: Partida contra a Holanda, nesta segunda-feira (16), marca o fim de uma parceria de 77 anos. A partir de 2027, a Nike assumirá o posto em um contrato de R$ 633 milhões por ano.
articles.body:
Nike em Pequim, China — Foto: REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

Após 77 anos e quatro títulos mundiais, Federação Alemã de Futebol (DFB) troca fornecedora compatriota pela Nike como fornecedora de material esportivo.

Acordo recorde contrasta com a crise vivida pela nova parceira. Em 4 de julho de 1954, no intervalo da final da Copa do Mundo na Suíça, no Estádio Wankdorf, em Berna, o placar entre Alemanha e Hungria estava em 2 a 2.

Chovia bastante naquela tarde. Foi quando o responsável pelo material esportivo da seleção alemã, Adolf Dassler, resolveu colocar travas mais altas nas chuteiras dos jogadores, melhorando a aderência no gramado escorregadio.

No segundo tempo, com um gol no final sacramentando a vitória, a Alemanha se tornava campeã mundial. O resto é história.

A narrativa em torno do primeiro dos quatro títulos mundiais da Alemanha tem um personagem importante, marcado pelas três listras icônicas: a Adidas. Para a empresa, o "milagre" na Suíça marcou o início de um sucesso empresarial global.

A fornecedora de artigos esportivos de Dassler ganhou impulso e, hoje, ocupa a segunda posição no mercado mundial, atrás apenas da gigante americana Nike.

No entanto, após 77 anos, a Federação Alemã de Futebol (DFB)encerrará sua parceria com a Adidas ao final deste ano. Nesta segunda-feira (16), no Estádio Olímpico de Berlim, a seleção da Alemanha se despede das três listras, no clássico contra a Holanda, pela Liga das Nações.

A partir de 2027, a Nike assumirá o posto, pagando, segundo informações, € 100 milhões (R$ 633 milhões) por ano, em um contrato de oito anos.

Tentativa desesperada de salvar a parceria

O fim da parceria foi um duro golpe para a empresa sediada na cidade de Herzogenaurach, no sul da Alemanha. Pouco antes da assinatura do contrato com a Nike, o CEO da Adidas, Björn Gulden, chegou a viajar para Frankfurt, em uma operação de última hora, com a missão de salvar a parceria de quase oito décadas. O esforço, porém, foi em vão.

A notícia do acordo com a Nike, em março de 2024, virou questão de Estado. O então ministro da Economia e vice-chanceler federal, Robert Habeck (do Partido Verde), disse, à ocasião, ter sentido falta de um "patriotismo local" alemão com a mudança.

O então ministro da Saúde, Karl Lauterbach, do Partido Social-Democrata (SPD), classificou a decisão como um erro que destruía um pedaço da identidade nacional. O atual chanceler federal da Alemanha, Friedrich Merz, da União Democrata Cristã (CDU), também descreveu a atitude da DFB como "não patriótica".

A federação, no entanto, não tinha outra escolha, pois precisa de dinheiro. Atualmente, a situação é tratada de maneira menos emocional. Talvez isso se deva ao fato de a seleção nacional vir decepcionando em todos os torneios há anos.

No mercado global, existem atualmente equipes mais atraentes. A camisa preta com listras verticais douradas, criada para a despedida, já está sendo vendida com um desconto de 25%.

A chegada da Nike tem um histórico. Em 2007, a empresa encaminhou uma oferta de 500 milhões de euros, que a DFB recusou. Um ano antes, a obrigatoriedade do uso de calçados de uma marca específica havia sido revogada na federação.

Os jogadores da seleção não precisavam mais usar chuteiras da Adidas em partidas internacionais. Isso também foi considerado um marco.

Evento de despedida com o técnico Jürgen Klopp

Na semana passada, em um evento descontraído para funcionários em Herzogenaurach, Gulden se despediu da seleção alemã e do técnico Jürgen Klopp, ele próprio um garoto-propaganda da Adidas.

"Nada de negatividade", pediu o CEO norueguês, acrescentando que todos na empresa continuariam sendo torcedores.

O uso, por parte de Klopp, de um boné da Adidas com a inscrição " Um entre 83 milhões " – uma referência à população da Alemanha – impulsionou as vendas desde sua estreia no comando da equipe, em setembro.

O técnico espera que as vendas de última hora de seu icônico boné ajudem a Alemanha e a Adidas a encerrarem sua relação com chave de ouro, ao mesmo tempo em que já pensa em novas ideias para quando a Nike assumir, em janeiro.

"Bem, o Natal vem antes disso. Ouvi dizer que muita gente vai ganhar o boné de presente de Natal", afirmou.

Klopp disse que pretende continuar usando bonés no futuro, já que, segundo ele, "assim não é preciso se preocupar com o cabelo", e espera chegar a um acordo com a Nike sobre um tema adequado.

"Veremos se, no ano que vem, haverá alguma mensagem em torno da qual todos nós possamos nos unir", disse o treinador.

A Alemanha entrou em campo pela primeira vez em um grande torneio com as famosas três listras na Eurocopa de 1980, na Itália. Mas isso só aconteceu na final, já que, na fase de grupos, a equipe jogou com camisas da marca Erima. Embora a seleção campeã mundial de 1974 também usasse Adidas, a marca não ficava visível.

Desde esse torneio, no entanto, a Adidas forneceu os uniformes da DFB, criando peças que ficariam na memória dos torcedores e dos fãs do futebol.

Em 2004, o então técnico da seleção, Jürgen Klinsmann, optou por um uniforme reserva vermelho, visando um estilo de jogo mais agressivo. Já a camisa reserva rosa para a Eurocopa de 2024, realizada na Alemanha, gerou polêmica.

Porém, segundo a Adidas, essa acabou sendo a camisa reserva mais vendida do selecionado germânico.

Para a empresa, o futebol, mesmo sem a DFB como parceira, continua sendo, de longe, a modalidade esportiva mais rentável. O mercado alemão é relevante, representando uma participação de faturamento na faixa média de um dígito do faturamento total. Ainda assim, espera-se que os impactos econômicos da perda permaneçam em um patamar administrável.

A companhia fornece uniformes para as seleções nacionais de 25 países, incluindo grandes potências do futebol como Itália, Argentina e México. Ainda mais estratégicos para a Adidas são os contratos com clubes como Real Madrid, Liverpool e Arsenal.

Somam-se a isso seis clubes da primeira divisão do futebol alemão, a Bundesliga – liderados pelo Bayern de Munique – e contratos individuais com alguns dos melhores jogadores do mundo, como Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal e Ousmane Dembélé.

Enquanto a Adidas registrou recentemente recordes financeiros, a Nike atravessa uma crise. Com queda no faturamento e nos lucros, recuo nas vendas em mercados importantes como a China e ações em desvalorização, a líder do setor está sendo forçada a adotar um rigoroso plano de corte de gastos.

Centenas de postos de trabalho devem ser eliminados.

Devido aos maus resultados financeiros, o CEO da Nike, John Donahoe – responsável por fechar o contrato recorde com a DFB –, teve que deixar o cargo em 2024. O acordo de € 800 milhões (R$ 5 bilhões) com a DFB, válido até o final de 2034, parece, no momento, destoar da atual realidade da Nike.

Outras seleções parceiras, como Brasil, Inglaterra, França e Portugal, provavelmente exigirão valores semelhantes em futuras negociações contratuais.

Além dos uniformes e acessórios da seleção alemã, a Nike anunciou nesta segunda-feira que fornecerá as bolas oficiais para as competições da União das Associações Europeias de Futebol (Uefa), como a Liga dos Campeões masculina, a Liga Europa, a Liga Conferência e a Supercopa da Europa, até 2031.

A Adidas fornecia as bolas para a entidade que rege o futebol europeu, desde 2001.

O novo visual das seleções da DFB ainda é mantido sob sigilo absoluto. Durante a Copa do Mundo de 2026, nos Estados Unidos, uma ação de marketing de guerrilha gerou um certo alvoroço. Um barco navegando pelo rio Hudson, em Nova York, exibia um banner com o jogador Jamal Musiala.

Na imagem, a estrela do Bayern vestia uma camisa bastante pixelada, mas que trazia o famoso símbolo da Nike.

Recentemente, torcedores discutiram na internet imagens vazadas de um suposto uniforme com um design clássico da DFB: branco, com gola preta e logotipo prateado.

No domingo, a seleção alemã utilizou pela última vez as luxuosas instalações em Herzogenaurach para o treino final antes da última partida da fase de grupos da Liga das Nações contra a Holanda.

Em seguida, a equipe viajou para Berlim, onde, nesta segunda-feira, buscará uma vitória para garantir sua vaga nas quartas de final do torneio europeu de seleções.

articles.title: Pacote fiscal: Alckmin diz que não há razão para oscilação do mercado | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta segunda, dólar fechou em alta, cotado a R$ 5,7767. Parte do mercado considera medidas previstas no pacote fiscal do governo insuficientes para conter o avanço da dívida pública.
articles.summary: Geraldo Alckmin defende o pacote fiscal do governo e minimiza a alta do dólar, afirmando que o Brasil tem segurança jurídica e trabalha para atingir o superávit.
articles.body:
O presidente em exercício, Geraldo Alckmin , afirmou nesta segunda-feira (16) que não há razão para as oscilações do mercado financeiro após o governo ter apresentado na semana passada pacote que reúne medidas para conter gastos e melhorar as contas públicas, com impacto estimado em até R$ 60 bilhões em 2027.

Nesta segunda, o dólar fechou em alta de 2,15%, cotado a R$ 5,7767 . Na máxima do dia, chegou a R$ 5,7949, maior valor desde 17 de abril de 2025, quando encerrou a R$ 5,8042. O Ibovespa, principal índice da bolsa brasileira, caía 2,11% por volta das 17h, aos 168.827 pontos.

"Não há razão para o mercado ter essas oscilações. O Brasil é uma das maiores economias do mundo, tem reservas internacionais, inflação sob controle, segurança jurídica, então não há razão para essas oscilações. Acredito que serão passageiras e o Brasil está trabalhando para não ter déficit e fazer superávit primário", afirmou Alckmin.

A fala do presidente em exercício ocorreu após se reunir com entidades que lançaram um manifesto contra supersalários.

O movimento reflete as preocupações dos investidores com as contas públicas brasileiras, após a aprovação do texto-base do projeto fiscal do governo na semana passada. Parte do mercado considera as medidas insuficientes para conter o avanço da dívida pública.

O cenário externo também pressionou os mercados brasileiros, em meio à maior cautela dos investidores. Eles estão menos dispostos a assumir riscos enquanto aguardam a divulgação de balanços de grandes empresas, especialmente da Nvidia.

Alckmin afirmou ainda que o governo já está tomando medidas para acalmar o mercado e que caso o Congresso faça alterações no projeto que prevê ajuste fiscal, a redução dos gastos, prevista para cerca de R$ 60 bilhões, "não cairá significativamente".

"Se aprovar o texto aprovado pelo Senado , ele é um avanço. Ele está na direção correta para a gente zerar o déficit, cumprir o acordo, o arcabouço fiscal e caminhar para ter superávit. Porque será com superávit que nós vamos reduzir o endividamento frente ao PIB. Então o governo já está trabalhando, já está fazendo essas oscilações. O mercado é assim mesmo, mas não vejo razão sólida para isso se manter", afirmou.

Na semana passada, o governo enviou ao Senado um projeto de lei complementar de ajuste das contas públicas. Entre as medidas estão a revisão de benefícios fiscais e a contenção de despesas (veja mais abaixo) .

A equipe econômica quer aprovar as medidas para tentar cumprir a meta fiscal de 2027 : um superávit de R$ 73 bilhões.

O projeto, apresentado pelo senador Jaques Wagner (PT-BA), teve seu texto-base aprovado pelo Senado, mas a votação ainda não foi concluída . Os senadores precisam analisar quatro destaques que podem alterar a proposta. Só depois o texto seguirá para a Câmara dos Deputados.

Com corte linear de 10% nos benefícios fiscais e mudanças no cálculo de pisos de gastos, o texto enfrentou resistência de senadores da oposição.

💵 O ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, afirmou que o conjunto de medidas poderá reduzir entre R$ 50 bilhões e R$ 60 bilhões em gastos no orçamento de 2027 .

O governo tem pressa para aprovar o texto para que as regras já possam estar em vigor para o próximo ano.

Geraldo Alckmin, vice-presidente da República. — Foto: Júlio César Silva/MDIC

articles.title: Apple é investigada no Cade por barrar PIX por aproximação no iPhone; entenda a disputa  | G1
articles.standfirst: Bancos e fintechs acusam a fabricante de restringir o acesso à tecnologia NFC e cobrar tarifas que dificultam pagamentos fora do Apple Pay. Empresa nega impedir a concorrência e defende as exigências de segurança.
articles.summary: Investigação apura se restrições da Apple ao acesso à tecnologia de pagamentos por aproximação favorecem o Apple Pay e dificultam a oferta do PIX por bancos e fintechs em iPhones.
articles.body:
Polícia mapeou valor do prejuízo após analisar transferências via PIX do suspeito — Foto: Bruno Peres/Agência Brasil/Arquivo

O Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) investiga se a Apple impõe barreiras que dificultam a oferta do PIX por aproximação por bancos e fintechs nos iPhones.

A suspeita é que as restrições ao acesso à tecnologia usada nesse tipo de pagamento favoreçam o Apple Pay, carteira digital da própria empresa, e prejudiquem empresas concorrentes no mercado de pagamentos móveis. Procurada pelo g1 , a Apple não respondeu até a publicação desta reportagem.

No centro da disputa está a tecnologia NFC (Near Field Communication), que permite a troca de informações entre dispositivos próximos. É ela que possibilita, por exemplo, pagar uma compra apenas aproximando o celular de uma maquininha.

A investigação foi aberta pela Superintendência-Geral do Cade, responsável pela apuração inicial de possíveis infrações às regras de concorrência. O inquérito administrativo, de número 08700.002893/2025-17, busca esclarecer se as condições técnicas e comerciais impostas pela Apple dificultam o acesso de empresas concorrentes à tecnologia NFC dos iPhones.

A controvérsia envolve a Zetta, associação que reúne fintechs como Nubank, Mercado Pago e PicPay, e a Federação Brasileira de Bancos (Febraban). As entidades pedem que a Apple permita que desenvolvedores utilizem a tecnologia NFC sem cobranças que consideram restritivas à concorrência.

A Apple, por sua vez, nega no processo impedir o uso do NFC por terceiros. A empresa afirma que oferece alternativas para que outros aplicativos realizem pagamentos por aproximação e defende que suas exigências de segurança e as tarifas cobradas pelo uso da tecnologia são legítimas. (veja abaixo o que diz a empresa)

A Zetta e a Febraban afirmam que a Apple mantém o iOS, sistema operacional dos iPhones, fechado ao acesso de outras empresas à tecnologia NFC. Na avaliação das entidades, esse modelo favorece o Apple Pay, que seria a principal alternativa disponível para pagamentos por aproximação no aparelho.

A Febraban afirma que, atualmente, o Apple Pay é o único aplicativo autorizado a realizar pagamentos com cartões por aproximação nos dispositivos com iOS. Para a entidade, essa limitação pode encarecer os serviços e reduzir as opções disponíveis aos consumidores.

A Zetta também argumenta que as regras da Apple dificultam a oferta do PIX por aproximação nos aplicativos de bancos e fintechs.

"Atualmente, a Apple bloqueia as APIs necessárias para processar o Pix na tecnologia NFC e exige a utilização da sua própria plataforma paga", afirma a associação em sua manifestação ao CADE.

APIs são ferramentas que permitem a comunicação entre diferentes programas e serviços. Segundo a Zetta, as restrições técnicas e as tarifas cobradas pela Apple tornam a oferta do PIX por aproximação economicamente inviável para usuários de iPhone.

As entidades comparam o modelo da Apple ao do Android, sistema operacional usado por diferentes fabricantes de celulares. Segundo elas, no Android, desenvolvedores podem acessar gratuitamente a tecnologia NFC por meio de um recurso chamado HCE, que permite simular um cartão de pagamento usando o software do próprio celular.

Por isso, defendem que o Cade determine que a Apple permita o acesso de aplicativos de terceiros ao NFC dos iPhones, sem cobranças restritivas e nas mesmas condições oferecidas à sua própria carteira digital.

A Zetta também cita o exemplo da União Europeia, onde a Apple se comprometeu a permitir que desenvolvedores acessem a tecnologia NFC sem custos.

A Apple contesta as acusações e afirma que não impede o uso da tecnologia NFC por outros desenvolvedores nos iPhones.

Segundo a empresa, existem duas maneiras de viabilizar pagamentos por aproximação no sistema: integrar cartões ao Apple Pay ou utilizar a plataforma NFC & SE, disponibilizada para aplicativos de terceiros a partir de outubro de 2024.

A empresa argumenta que a exigência do Secure Element (SE), componente de segurança presente nos aparelhos, é necessária para proteger os usuários contra fraudes e programas maliciosos.

Na avaliação da Apple, esse modelo oferece mais proteção do que o HCE, defendido pela Zetta. Isso porque o Secure Element utiliza um componente físico separado para proteger os dados das transações, enquanto o HCE simula o funcionamento de um cartão por meio de um software executado no processador principal do celular.

A empresa também defende seu direito de cobrar pelo uso da tecnologia e da infraestrutura de segurança que oferece. Para a Apple, as tarifas compensam os investimentos em engenharia e não representam uma prática ilegal.

Outro argumento da companhia é que o NFC não é indispensável para a concorrência no mercado brasileiro de pagamentos presenciais.

Em manifestação ao Cade, a empresa apresentou dados do Banco Central referentes a setembro de 2026. Segundo os números citados pela Apple, foram realizadas aproximadamente 2,09 milhões de transações de PIX por aproximação, contra cerca de 3,14 bilhões de operações com QR Codes dinâmicos no mesmo período.

Com esses dados, a companhia argumenta que os consumidores já contam com alternativas amplamente utilizadas e que a abertura do NFC não seria necessária para garantir a concorrência no setor.

A Superintendência-Geral do Cade ainda precisa concluir a análise das informações reunidas. Até o momento, o órgão não decidiu se a Apple cometeu alguma infração às regras de concorrência.

Após analisar os argumentos das entidades do setor financeiro e a defesa da Apple, a Superintendência-Geral poderá decidir pela abertura de um processo administrativo ou pelo arquivamento do caso.

articles.title: Incertezas sobre a política fiscal aumentam a tensão no mercado financeiro | G1
articles.standfirst: O dólar alcança a maior cotação desde abril de 2025 e a bolsa fechou em forte queda.
articles.summary: O dólar alcança a maior cotação desde abril de 2025 e a bolsa fechou em forte queda.
articles.body:
As incertezas com os rumos das contas públicas fizeram o dólar disparar nesta segunda-feira (16). A bolsa de valores caiu quase 2%.

Às 9h, uma hora antes da abertura dos negócios na bolsa, saíram dados econômicos ruins. O Banco Central mostrou que a atividade econômica do país encolheu 0,2% em setembro. Com isso, o índice que é considerado uma prévia do PIB terminou o terceiro trimestre com queda de 0,9%. Além disso, a pesquisa que o BC faz semanalmente com o mercado financeiro captou uma piora de expectativas para 2027. A previsão de crescimento do PIB caiu para 1,02%. A previsão de inflação em 2027, que vem subindo a cada rodada da pesquisa, chegou agora a 5%. E o mercado financeiro também passou a esperar juros maiores em 2027.

Foi nesse clima que o pregão abriu. O Ibovespa caiu logo nos primeiros minutos e perdeu ainda mais força ao longo do dia. Fechou com queda de quase 2%, aos 169.000 pontos. Analistas do mercado disseram que o que mais pesou foi a avaliação de que o ajuste fiscal proposto pelo governo não vai conseguir reverter tantas projeções negativas.

"Existe uma métrica muito comum que o mercado usa que é a relação da dívida-PIB. E a gente está em um patamar já considerado não confortável, com uma perspectiva de piora. Então, essas percepções futuras foram se acumulando e esse pacote apresentado, apresentado dias atrás, aos olhos do mercado ele é considerado insuficiente frente ao desafio fiscal que o Brasil tem nos próximos anos", diz Otávio Oliveira, gerente de Tesouraria do bacno Daycoval.

Também pesa a indefinição sobre os nomes da próxima equipe econômica.

"Quem que vai ser o cabeça da pasta? Quem é que vai ditar as regras? E o tempo está correndo, ele o mercado não tá mais dando o benefício da dúvida", afirma Rodrigo Moliterno, sócio da Veedha Investimentos.

Incertezas sobre a política fiscal aumentam a tensão no mercado financeiro — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O presidente em exercício, Geraldo Alckmin , veio a público para tentar acalmar os ânimos sobre o ajuste fiscal:

"Não há razão para o mercado ter essas oscilações. O Brasil é uma das maiores economias do mundo. O Brasil tem reservas internacionais de mais de R$ 1,5 trilhão. O Brasil tem inflação sob controle. O Brasil tem segurança jurídica. Então, não há razão para essas oscilações, acredito que elas serão passageiras, e está trabalhando para não termos déficit e fazer superávit primário".

As mesmas razões que fizeram a bolsa cair levaram o dólar às alturas. É que, como reforçam os especialistas, a moeda americana é para onde os investidores fogem em momentos de muita incerteza. Nesta segunda-feira (16), o dólar subiu mais de 2% e fechou a R$ 5,77. É a maior cotação desde abril de 2027. Entre as 31 moedas mais negociadas no mundo, o real teve a maior desvalorização frente à moeda americana.

"O dólar remete à credibilidade. Então, o investidor, quando ele busca mais o dólar, significa que a expectativa de uma solução ou a credibilidade com o país está muito menor. Então, ele já não quer mais investir no país, ele já busca uma talvez uma saída, então, se proteger. E, logicamente, fora isso, você tem o dólar como também um um fator de custo. Quanto mais elevado o dólar, mais impacto também na inflação você tem", afirma Rodrigo Moliterno.

articles.summary: Gold price prediction today: The technical bias for gold prices continues to be bearish in the near-term, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity
articles.body: Gold price prediction today: The technical bias for gold prices continues to be bearish in the near-term, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Here’s what he has to say:Gold continues to remain under pressure, after extending its decline from the November highs around Rs 145,000-146,000. The 15-minute chart indicates a sustained bearish structure, with prices consistently forming lower highs and lower lows. Gold is trading below its 20-period average near Rs 136,349, while the Bollinger Bands are positioned at Rs 137,070 on the upside and Rs 135,627 on the downside.The recent consolidation around Rs 136,000-136,500 has failed to generate a meaningful recovery, and the latest move towards the lower Bollinger Band indicates that selling pressure remains dominant. Immediate support is placed around Rs 135,500-135,600, followed by Rs 134,500 and Rs 133,000. A sustained break below Rs 135,500 could extend the decline towards these levels. On the upside, Rs 136,350 is the first hurdle, followed by Rs 137,000-137,100.A sustained recovery above Rs 137,100 could trigger short-covering towards Rs 138,000-139,000. However, the broader short-term structure is unlikely to improve meaningfully unless prices reclaim Rs 139,000-140,000. Overall, the technical bias remains bearish, with any recovery likely to encounter selling pressure near the immediate resistance zones.Gold and silver extended their decline during the week, with bullion falling nearly 4.5% and touching a more-than-one-year low, while silver declined approximately 3%, reflecting broad-based weakness across precious metals. Persistent inflation concerns, a stronger US dollar and increasingly hawkish Fed expectations continued to weigh on investor sentiment.The latest US producer price data added to these concerns, with October PPI recording its largest annual increase in four years, reinforcing the view that inflationary pressures remain persistent despite earlier expectations of moderation.Following stronger employment and consumer inflation readings, markets have increasingly priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, with the possibility of further monetary tightening extending into early 2027. This has kept real yields elevated and increased the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.The US dollar index hovering around 103.5 has added another layer of pressure, making gold more expensive for overseas buyers and limiting international investment demand.Meanwhile, expectations of a prolonged restrictive monetary-policy environment have encouraged investors to reassess exposure to precious metals following their substantial earlier rally.The correction in silver has been particularly pronounced, reflecting its dual exposure to investment sentiment and industrial demand. Concerns surrounding China’s economic performance have also weighed on the metal, as uncertainty over manufacturing activity and industrial consumption raises questions about the strength of physical demand.Energy-market developments have offered some relief to the broader inflation outlook. The International Energy Agency’s assessment of improving global oil supply, despite continuing geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions, has eased concerns over persistent crude-market tightness.Moderating energy prices could gradually reduce inflationary pressure and provide the Federal Reserve with greater flexibility, although the immediate impact on gold remains limited by elevated rate expectations. Investors are also closely monitoring Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments and the upcoming FOMC minutes for further clarity on the policy trajectory.Any indication that policymakers remain concerned about persistent inflation could reinforce expectations of another rate increase, while a more balanced assessment could help stabilise bullion.Overall, the near-term outlook remains cautious as persistent inflation, dollar strength and expectations of further monetary tightening continue to outweigh gold’s safe-haven appeal.The possibility of additional rate increases into early 2027 remains a significant headwind. However, any moderation in inflation expectations, softer Treasury yields or renewed investment demand could provide opportunities for stabilisation following the sharp correction.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.body: Symbiosis International (Deemed University) announces the closing of its registration window for the Symbiosis National Aptitude (SNAP) Test 2026 on 25th November 2026 (Wednesday). The registration fee is Rs. 2,550 per attempt, with an additional Rs. 1,000 per programme.The final selection process (merit listing) is based on a composite score that includes:SNAP Score (scaled to 50 marks)Group Exercise (10 marks)Personal Interaction (40 marks)Total: 100 MarksEligible candidates must hold a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university/institution of national importance with at least 50% marks (45% for SC/ST). articles.title: Anthropic is eyeing a mega IPO, but will investors buy its trillion-dollar AI dream?
articles.summary: Will Anthropic's IPO be a market blockbuster or another case of early fireworks fading fast?
articles.body: Will Anthropic's IPO be a market blockbuster or another case of early fireworks fading fast?The Claude parent’s proposed $1.4 trillion listing comes at a time when recent technology IPOs have delivered sharply contrasting returns, leaving investors with little indication of what could lie ahead.An analysis by S&P Global Market Intelligence of seven major recent US technology IPOs found that four were trading above their offer prices a year after listing, while the other three had suffered significant losses. The contrasting returns offer little certainty about how Anthropic's shares will perform if its proposed Nasdaq listing goes ahead.The AI company plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece, according to an amended registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10. At the upper end of the price band, the offering could fetch $64.35 billion, placing Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at around $1.4 trillion. Its shares are expected to trade under the ticker ANT.This would put the company above its $965 billion valuation from a May funding round, although below the approximately $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for earlier this year.Tech IPO scorecard: Big gains, bigger setbacksThe first-year performance of recent listings has been far from uniform. Arm Holdings topped the S&P analysis, delivering a 171.4 per cent return after its September 2023 listing. Snowflake and Airbnb were not far behind, gaining 169.6 per cent and 165.3 per cent, respectively. DoorDash also posted a positive return of 61.6 per cent.The picture was less encouraging for Lyft, Uber and Rivian. Their shares fell 62.6 per cent, 29.7 per cent and 57.7 per cent, respectively, amid market disruptions and rising interest rates.Even some of the biggest recent offerings have struggled to maintain their initial momentum. SpaceX, which raised $135 per share in June in the largest IPO on record, witnessed a surge in its stock during the first two trading sessions. However, the rally subsequently lost steam.On June 18, its shares dropped 6.5 per cent as investors booked profits and weighed the company's high valuation against the costs of expanding its AI operations. By November 11, the stock was 13.2 per cent below its offer price, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix also saw early gains give way to a correction after its Nasdaq debut in July. Its American depositary receipts (ADRs), which were priced at $149, rose 12.8 per cent on the first trading day before falling nearly 8 per cent on the second as investors booked profits.Revenue is soaring, but so are the costsAnthropic's financial numbers present another important consideration ahead of its proposed market debut. The company reported revenue of $33.24 billion in the first nine months of 2026, significantly higher than the $4.58 billion recorded for the whole of 2025.Its third-quarter revenue stood at around $17 billion, registering a 47 per cent increase over the previous quarter. However, the revenue growth comes alongside substantial losses and infrastructure spending.Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. Its infrastructure commitments stood at around $895 billion, including $69.8 billion payable within 12 months.More shares could enter the market from day oneThe number of shares available for trading could also become a point of focus after the listing. Anthropic's employees and early investors will be allowed to sell some of their holdings from the first day of trading, instead of being bound by the standard 180-day lock-up period.There is also another component to the IPO's funding arrangements. Seven of the company's computing suppliers have agreed to buy a combined $26 billion worth of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price.AI investment faces the returns questionAnthropic's proposed debut comes as investors take a closer look at whether massive investments in artificial intelligence are translating into revenue at the pace expected.Recent third-quarter earnings have brought capital expenditure and the ability of companies to generate returns from AI spending into sharper focus. Regulatory uncertainty following the US midterm elections has added another concern for the sector.With recent technology listings showing that first-day excitement does not always guarantee sustained stock market gains, Anthropic's proposed IPO will bring its valuation, financial losses and infrastructure commitments under investor scrutiny.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: In 2020, Delhi Metro launched the first driverless trains; six years on, 1.6 million rode them in a day, more than Arunachal Pradesh’s population and one in five of its 8 million daily passengers.
articles.summary: In 2020, Delhi Metro launched the first set of its driverless trains on the Magenta Line.
articles.body: In 2020, Delhi Metro launched the first set of its driverless trains on the Magenta Line. Almost six years later, the driverless trains are an integral part of the Delhi Metro network as ridership grows in the country’s biggest metro network.Delhi Metro currently operates 100 Unattended Train Operation (UTO) trains over 120 km of its Magenta and Pink lines. This is 29% of the network, a share that is expected to grow as the driverless network expands to 198 km after ongoing projects are completed.Delhi Metro got driverless trains in December 2020Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched India’s first driverless train services on the Delhi Metro’s Magenta Line, which runs between Janakpuri West and Botanical Garden, on 28 December 2020.The driverless trains operate through a fully automated system, removing the possibility of human error. Following the introduction of driverless services on the Magenta Line, the Delhi Metro’s Pink Line adopted these trains as well.1.6 million travel by driverless trainsDelhi Metro’s driverless trains carried a staggering 1.6 million passengers in a single day on November 2 this year, as commuters travelled in large numbers ahead of Diwali.This meant that one in every five of the network’s eight million daily passengers used a driverless train!The number is more than Arunachal Pradesh’s entire population, according to the 2011 Census, according to an ET analysis.Driverless metro trains across India?Vikas Kumar, managing director of Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), believes the time has come for other metro rail projects to adopt this model."Driverless train operations bring more flexibility to train operations, reducing human intervention and human errors. They also help improve the availability of coaches for service," Kumar told ET.He added that the reliability of Delhi’s driverless trains had improved manifold because of exhaustive self-tests carried out before the trains entered service, helping eliminate human errors.The technology, however, has its critics, including some within the government. They cite the higher initial capital expenditure required for driverless operations and the possibility that train drivers could become redundant.Sudhanshu Mani, the former railway general manager who played a key role in developing the Vande Bharat train prototype in 2018, has warned against India adopting driverless train technology without assessing its suitability for the country.While automation is increasingly becoming the global preference for new metro projects, he believes India should base its decisions on its own requirements rather than simply follow the international trend."In India, with much lower staffing costs compared to the developed world, our own analysis instead of the global trend should dictate our decision," he told the financial daily.Mani acknowledged that driverless operations offer several operational benefits. "Automation eliminates human error, guarantees precise arrival and departure schedules, and frees up additional passenger space where the driver's cabin would normally sit," he said.However, a conclusive comparison of the costs and benefits of driverless and conventional metro systems is not readily available.Responding to concerns that automation could eliminate the need for train drivers, DMRC managing director Vikas Kumar said none of the operators who stopped driving trains after driverless services were introduced in 2020 had lost their jobs. Instead, they were assigned other responsibilities within the organisation.DMRC currently employs around 3,000 train operators. Across India, metro rail services are running in 26 cities, including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Chennai, Lucknow, Pune and Ahmedabad."They have been strategically deputed for tasks such as station management, crowd control etc.," he added.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Lakshmi Venu challenges TVS family settlement,  seeks partition of father's assets
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of industrialist Venu Srinivasan, has formally sought a partition of the assets belonging to her father's branch of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of industrialist Venu Srinivasan, has formally sought a partition of the assets belonging to her father's branch of the TVS family, claiming an equal share under the Hindu Succession Act.The move has escalated a succession dispute over the distribution of family wealth and beneficial interests in several businesses, including TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton, news agency PTI reported.In a partition notice sent to her father, Lakshmi called on him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary responsibilities and ensure a "fair and lawful partition". She has invoked Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, which recognises daughters as coparceners with the same rights and liabilities as sons in Hindu joint family property.Also check: Venu Srinivasan family business dispute escalates to Chennai court as both sides file caveatsHer mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has backed the demand, arguing that a daughter is entitled to an equal share in family assets.While Venu Srinivasan and his son Sudarshan maintain that a settlement has already been reached, Lakshmi and Mallika contend that there has been no comprehensive division of the family's economic assets. Lakshmi has argued that the earlier arrangements dealt with business control and the use of family trademarks, but did not settle the ownership and distribution of the underlying assets.The assets and interests in question are held through family trusts and corporate structures, including the VS Trust. TVS Holdings' annual report shows that the family and promoter group hold 74.45% of the company, with Venu Srinivasan holding 66.55% through the VS Trust. TVS Holdings, in turn, owns a 56% stake in TVS Motor Company."Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India," Lakshmi said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: EU slaps anti-dumping duties on steel imports from India, 4 other countries
articles.summary: The European Union on Monday imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of cold-rolled flat steel from India and four other countries, with rates
articles.body: The European Union on Monday imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of cold-rolled flat steel from India and four other countries, with rates ranging from 3% to 27.9%. This follows an investigation that found the products were being sold in the EU at dumped prices.India faces a duty of 9.5%, while Japan has been hit with the highest rate of 27.9%. The duties on Taiwan range from 20.7% to 27%, those on Türkiye from 3% to 7.8%, and Vietnam faces a 16% duty.The European Commission said the investigation was significant because it was the first in which it established the existence of what it calls “particular market situations” in some of the countries under investigation. It said the findings could have wider implications for the EU's trade defence measures.Why India and Taiwan were flaggedThe Commission established particular market situations in India and Taiwan, saying domestic market conditions in both countries affected the prices used to assess whether steel was being dumped in the EU.In India's case, it found that government measures had affected domestic iron ore prices. Iron ore is a key raw material used in the production of cold-rolled flat steel, as per an EU report.For Taiwan, the Commission cited the impact of Chinese overcapacity. It said increased imports of cold-rolled flat steel from China had put downward pressure on domestic prices and weakened profitability for Taiwanese producers.Under EU anti-dumping rules, the Commission can construct a product's normal value instead of relying on domestic selling prices when it finds that market conditions do not allow a proper comparison between domestic and export prices.The Commission said it had taken corrective measures and that the investigation revealed the full extent of dumping in the EU market.Scale of EU steel marketCold-rolled flat steel is used across several manufacturing sectors. The EU market for these products is valued at around 23.2 billion euros, with domestic production spread across 12 member countries and employing more than 8,600 people.The Commission's statement puts the value of imports from the five countries at 1.072 billion euros. Taiwan accounted for 345 million euros, followed by India at 282 million euros, Türkiye at 240 million euros, Japan at 180 million euros and Vietnam at 125 million euros.The EU said the duties are intended to protect its domestic steel industry from trade-distorting practices.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia faces extraordinary push to restore Huang days after his exit
articles.summary: By Jaspreet Singh and Ross Kerber Nov 16 (Reuters) - Four days after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, felled by revelations of affairs including one with a...
articles.body:
Nov 16 (Reuters) - Four days after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia , felled by revelations of affairs including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, an extraordinary campaign is underway to restore him to the helm of the company he built.

More than 180,200 people have signed a petition demanding Huang's return, Elon ‌Musk has thrown his support behind the effort, and U.S. President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang reinstated as CEO. Thousands of people identifying themselves as Nvidia employees ‌have joined the call, even as governance experts and some investors warn that bringing him back before investigations are complete could expose the company to fresh risks.

The groundswell of support for Huang has turned a corporate succession story into a test of whether ​Nvidia can separate itself from a founder whose influence stretches across its employees — some fiercely loyal to the former CEO — and shareholders, Silicon Valley, the Taiwan supply chain and Washington.

Taiwan's tallest skyscraper, Taipei 101, was illuminated on Monday with messages including "Taiwan Loves Jensen." Some prominent shareholders such as Atreides Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital Management CEO Brad Gerstner have urged Nvidia not to rush to replace him before all the facts were known.

The support for the former CEO comes as U.S. intelligence agencies are still trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's relationship with China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two ‌sources familiar with the matter. Evidence gathered so far indicates she was ⁠likely an intelligence asset, someone who shared information, rather than a fully trained spy, the sources said.

But Nvidia's board was not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The uncertainty has divided investors over Huang's future and complicated the board's search for a successor. Nvidia shares fell 3.7% ⁠on Monday, a day before the chipmaker is due third-quarter earnings.

The "Stand With Jensen" campaign listed SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney among its signatories.

The campaign website showed more than 8,800 signatories identified themselves as current Nvidia employees and more than 94,000 as shareholders, though it cautioned that professional affiliations were self-reported and had not been independently verified.

articles.title: The S&P 500's shot at 4 straight double-digit years is in Nvidia's hands
articles.summary: Nvidia's earnings could decide whether the S&P 500 notches a rare fourth straight double-digit year.
articles.body:
Stocks are within reach of their fourth straight year of double-digit gains, the first since the 1990s dot-com boom. Apple ( AAPL ) is doing the heavy lifting, while Nvidia ( NVDA ) could still cost the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) its four-peat.

The S&P 500 closed Monday up about 8% for 2026, roughly 110 points shy of the 7,530 or so it needs to end the year with a 10% gain. It had just closed above that line as recently as Friday.

BofA's Michael Hartnett counts only three such streaks since 1871, according to a BofA Global Research report. Those came during World War II, right after it, and in the late-1990s internet boom, when the index "logged 5 straight years" of 10%-plus gains.

Apple has added about 125 points to the S&P 500 this year, more than any other stock, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Chipmakers Micron ( MU ) and AMD ( AMD ) come next, at about 50 points each.

Nvidia sits at the other end. Its slide has subtracted about 75 points, roughly two-thirds of the gap between Monday's close and the 10% line. Tesla ( TSLA ), Oracle ( ORCL ), and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) have each taken away about 25 to 40 points.

Nvidia reports its third quarter results after the close on Nov. 17, its first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO .

At about 6% of the index, according to Carson Group's Sonu Varghese, every 10% move in Nvidia is worth roughly 40 points. Even a big post-earnings jump couldn't close the roughly 110-point gap alone.

The rest of the market has already done its part. More than half of S&P 500 stocks are up at least 10% this year.

Since the S&P 500's Oct. 6 record, chip stocks have shed about $5.5 trillion in market value, more than the roughly $3.7 trillion the whole index has lost. Gains in Apple and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) have softened the blow.

"I don't think the stock market overall is expensive," Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman said at Yahoo Finance Invest . "I think there are a lot of stocks that have been obliterated and are at attractive valuations."

DoubleLine's Jeffrey Gundlach isn't buying it . He recommends "only 30% in equities" until the S&P 500's price-to-earnings ratio falls below 15.

Since 1928, the S&P 500 had been up 10% or more by mid-November in 45 years, and every one of them finished with a double-digit gain, by Yahoo Finance calculations. This year was in that club at Friday's close.

From here, the index needs to gain about 1.5% by Dec. 31. Since 1990, it has done that over the final six weeks in 20 of 36 years.

articles.title: Bank outage reports spike: JPMorgan says issues are resolved, blames internal software bug for transaction delays
articles.summary: Reports of bank app outages surged on Monday, sparking widespread alarm days after last week's major Microsoft Outlook outage.
articles.body:
Reports of problems with banking apps and payment services surged across major US banks Monday, though several institutions said their systems were operating as usual while some customers experienced transaction delays.

Customers' reports of issues spiked across a number of sites, including those for JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America ( BAC ), US Bank (USB), Wells Fargo ( WFC ), PNC ( PNC ), Citigroup ( C ), and Capital One ( COF ), according to outage aggregator Downdetector . Digital payment network Zelle, which is owned by Early Warning Services, also saw reports of customers experiencing issues.

Reports of problems began declining by Monday afternoon with complaints remaining elevated across several banks until the evening. Downdetector tracks user-submitted reports, which do not necessarily indicate outages at the financial institutions themselves.

JPMorgan Chase said a software bug affecting its internal hardware systems caused transaction delays Monday.

The nation's largest bank said the problem was not systemic, but acknowledged that other financial institutions may have experienced transaction delays when processing payments involving JPMorgan.

"This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," a JPMorgan spokesperson told Yahoo Finance.

The bank attributed the disruption to a "software bug in on-premise hardware systems," adding that there was no evidence the issue was related to a cyberattack. Customers continued to have access to their accounts and funds, the spokesperson said.

JPMorgan said Monday evening that it has resolved the issue.

Several other major US banks also saw a surge in customer outage reports on Monday. Some of the companies with reported service outages, acknowledged customer issues while saying they're operations were running as normal.

"U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays," a US Bank spokesperson said.

An Early Warning spokesperson said the payment network itself was in regular operation, despite some customers experiencing delays with payments made through the service.

"Zelle is not down. Zelle is operating as it should," the spokesperson said. "An issue at the financial institutions may be impacting broader services, including Zelle payments, for some of their customers," they added.

Other banks including Bank of America, PNC, Capital One and Truist whose customers reported issues said they were not experiencing disruptions.

Reports began to surface online Monday afternoon from customers across a range of banks saying they were receiving error messages when attempting to perform bank transactions. Chase said at around 4 p.m. on X that “JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware system” and that it was working to resolve it. The issues had been affecting both online and in-person branch transactions. The issue was not “cyber-related,” the bank said, and did not impact the entire banking system. “Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us.” The bank said that customers still had access to their accounts and funds, but some transactions were taking longer than normal. Regulators were in touch with the big banks affected “immediately,” a person familiar with the situation said earlier Monday. They “quickly determined this was contained and service was already in process of restoration,” the person said then. The issues at Chase were the latest in a series of nationwide tech glitches over the past week that have shaken public confidence in systems that tens of millions of Americans use every day. However, there is no evidence that these incidents are connected to one another. Microsoft Outlook went offline for approximately 48 hours last week due to what it called a capacity upgrade. On Friday, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for several hours over what U.S. officials said was a botched facilities upgrade. It was not immediately clear how many Chase accounts were affected by the glitch. The bank counts approximately 94 million customer relationships in the United States, with 5,000 physical branches and 15,000 ATMs. By late afternoon Monday, several Chase bank branches in Manhattan appeared to be operating normally. Customers leaving a branch at 6th Avenue and W. 51st Street told NBC News they didn’t know there had been a problem until they arrived at the branch, where they were told by employees that they’d gotten there at just the right time. “This is really retail banking,” and not tied to the rest of JPMorgan Chase, said a source familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak publicly. The issues with Chase accounts also appeared to be preventing customers from transferring money via Zelle. A representative for the company said that the technical issues on its platform originated with Chase. “Zelle is not down. Zelle is operating as it should,” the company told NBC News. “An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers. Please contact them directly.” A representative for U.S. Bank confirmed that Zelle customers were experiencing issues. “U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted,” the spokesman said. “However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.” A spokesperson for PNC Bank said it was “not experiencing any direct impact. We are aware of reports of transaction delays outside of the bank, but those appear to be resolving.” Truist bank said its services “are operating normally,We continue to closely monitor our systems and are not aware of any broad service disruptions at this time.” Customers at Wells Fargo also experienced delays, but the company did not provide a statement. Citibank likewise declined to comment. A spokesperson for Capital One said the bank “has not been impacted and continues to operate normally at this time.” — WMAQ’s Lauren Stauffer and Leigh Lesniak contributed reporting from Chicago.

articles.title: Thousands of Chase Bank customers report trouble with online banking services
articles.summary: Thousands of Chase Bank customers reported they had trouble using their online accounts on Monday.
articles.body: Thousands of Chase Bank customers reported they had trouble using their online accounts on Monday. “JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug,” a spokesperson said Monday. “It is taking longer than usual to service some customers.” The Chase spokesperson went on to say it was a “bug,” rather than a widespread cyberattack. Social media users reported issues with transactions at physical Chase branches, as well, and some local bank branches told customers earlier in the day that they were having issues with their internal system. However, Chase said in a statement that “customers still have access to their accounts and funds.” The outage wasn’t caused by a cloud-related issue or a cyber attack, a source familiar with the matter told CNN. Rather, an update on the company’s own physical computer systems inadvertently caused issues. As of 2:00 p.m. ET, more than 4,700 customers reported issues with Chase, according to Downdetector. Customers reported issues at other major banks, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and U.S. Bank, though on a smaller scale. The reports with the other banks appear to be related to sending money through Zelle, a digital payment network, to Chase accounts. “U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays,” U.S. Bank said in a statement. Zelle said that its service is “operating as it should.” The money-transferring service is owned by a consortium of US banks called Early Warning Services, and Zelle said it does not hold consumer funds. “An issue at the financial institutions may be impacting broader services, including Zelle payments, for some of their customers,” a Zelle spokesperson said. Chase also said it wasn’t a systemic issue. “Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us,” the spokesperson continued. Why systems keep failing Monday’s Chase outage marked the third straight weekday with a massive technical failure. On Thursday, a Microsoft outage cut off email access to millions of people across 74 countries and territories. On Friday, a Federal Aviation Administration systems failure led to a nationwide ground stop. And on Monday afternoon, United Airlines reported a systemwide computer problem that delayed flights. The incidents don’t share the same scope or root causes. Microsoft blamed a Windows defect, a traffic overload and capacity constraints. The FAA cited a router deployment issue and excessive data flooding its systems. It’s not yet clear what caused the Chase or United outages on Monday. But the glitches share a common theme: “the complexity and fragility of the systems that we depend on every day,” Mike Chapple, a professor of IT, Analytics, and Operations at the University of Notre Dame, said in emailed comments. “In each of these cases, what started as an issue in one small part of a larger system quickly spread, causing massive disruptions nationwide,” he added. Complexity and interdependence aren’t inherently flaws — in fact, they make systems more resilient, noted Rebecca Krauthamer, CEO and cofounder of QuSecure, a cryptography provider for the US government. “But when dependencies on systems aren’t sufficiently understood, failures can cascade across institutions and industries,” she added. Think about it like the Titanic: The watertight bulkheads were unable to withstand a failure that exceeded the ship’s architects’ worst-case-scenario assumptions. Even the best-designed systems sometimes succumb to threats and problems that the designers couldn’t have imagined when they built them. The problem with interdependent technology systems is that system failures are rarely isolated incidents: Our heavy reliance on a handful of systems means failures have tended to bring down systems across the world. “The question for leaders is not whether one system will fail but how many other things fail with it, and how fast you can contain it,” said Madhu Shashanka, founder of Concentric AI. articles.title: Should Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back, as Silicon Valley's elite are demanding?
articles.summary: The Jensen Huang debacle at Nvidia is heading into a new dimension.
articles.body:
Something pretty remarkable is happening in Silicon Valley right now. One shouldn't be surprised, considering the profit motives of many invested in the AI ecosystem and that what Nvidia ( NVDA ) does lies at the center of it all.

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as the company's CEO under a cloud of controversy he created, and suddenly some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley are organizing a campaign to bring him back.

Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk has signed on to the "Bring Jensen Back" petition. Other prominent executives have joined, including Uber ( UBER ) founder Travis Kalanick — who left Uber unceremoniously after his own string of highly publicized missteps.

The online petition has attracted more than 180,000 signatures. Nvidia employees have also taken to X and LinkedIn to voice their support for Huang.

Let's be clear: Jensen Huang is an extraordinary entrepreneur . A once-in-a-lifetime type of talent. He helped build Nvidia into one of the world's most important companies, with a market cap that neared $5 trillion earlier this year. His impact on the AI revolution is enormous and will not be forgotten.

But here's the issue a lot of people are right to point out: Being a brilliant CEO does not make you untouchable.

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

Huang admitted to being unfaithful to Lori, his wife of more than 40 years. There are serious questions surrounding his relationship with a reported Chinese spy. Additional reports say Jensen had affairs with two Nvidia employees, one of whom, Kimberly Powell , was a direct report.

All of these allegations and the broader circumstances deserve a thorough, independent investigation by the board and the law firm leading it, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. They should not be treated as proven facts.

This isn't just about one man's personal life. It's about corporate governance, national security, the responsibilities of a CEO, and the standards expected of someone running one of America's most strategically important companies.

Nvidia's board has a responsibility to shareholders, employees, and the country — not to Silicon Valley's celebrity CEO culture.

Jensen Huang absolutely deserves due process. But he is not bigger than Nvidia. And no CEO, no matter how brilliant, should be.

He said there were domestic requirements for more than 400 vessels, representing an investment opportunity of nearly $24 billion. articles.title: G7 economic optimism drops to Great Recession levels: Survey
articles.summary: Economic optimism among residents of Group of Seven (G7) countries has dipped to its lowest point since the late 2000s Great Recession, according to new polling data. The Gallup survey found that a median of 22 percent of G7 residents aged 15 and older said their local economic conditions were getting better, a decline of…
articles.body:
Economic optimism among residents of Group of Seven (G7) countries has dipped to its lowest point since the late 2000s Great Recession, according to new polling data.

The Gallup survey found that a median of 22 percent of G7 residents aged 15 and older said their local economic conditions were getting better, a decline of 13 percentage points from last year.

That marks the lowest median share of optimistic G7 residents since 2009, when a median of 21 percent said their local economic conditions were improving. The U.S., Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the U.K. make up the G7.

A median of two-thirds of respondents to the Gallup poll said their local economic conditions were worsening. The share of respondents who were pessimistic about the economy in their city area has spiked over the last decade, after it fell to 29 percent in 2017.

As recently as 2021, those who were optimistic about economic conditions, a median of 39 percent, roughly matched the pessimistic group, a median of 40 percent.

Americans’ concerns about the cost of living drove voters to punish President Trump and Republicans at the ballot box this midterm cycle , as Democrats swept control of both chambers of Congress.

Economic issues were front and center in the midterms, as inflation remains above 3 percent and energy and grocery prices have risen during the Iran war .

Nearly 9 in 10 voters told NBC News that the cost of living was either a “crucial” or “major” factor in determining their vote for Congress. Only about 1 in 10 voters said the cost of living was either a “minor” factor or not a factor.

A median of 29 percent of U.S. adults told Gallup this year their local economic conditions were improving, the third-highest share among G7 countries — behind Japan and Italy, respectively at 33 percent and 32 percent.

In France and the U.K., a median of 14 percent and 13 percent of residents, respectively, were optimistic about economic conditions.

Frustrations with the cost of living and France’s education and social services systems fueled widespread protests and riots in the European country this fall.

Gallup surveyed roughly 1,000 adults in each of the seven countries from April 6 to Aug. 29. The poll’s margin of error ranged between 3.5 and 4.1 percentage points.

articles.title: The biggest entertainment event of the year isn’t a movie — it’s ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
articles.summary: This week’s launch of “Grand Theft Auto VI” is arguably the biggest media and entertainment event of the year.
articles.body: This week’s launch of “Grand Theft Auto VI” is arguably the biggest media and entertainment event of the year. Some might even go further, since gamers have been waiting so long for Thursday’s release — the last “Grand Theft Auto” game came out in 2013 — and FOMO is kicking in among the general public. About 15 million copies of “GTA VI” have already been preordered, according to Sensor Tower data. Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss H. Zelnick told investors last week that the sales are at “unprecedented levels.” But if you’re not one of those gamers, you might not grasp why this is such a big business and cultural story. So I asked a couple of veteran video game industry journalists to put it into perspective. Peer Schneider, EVP and co-founder of IGN Entertainment, said, “It’s not a question of whether GTA VI will be a hit; it’s a question of just how big it’ll be.” “The last game in the series, GTA V, famously made a billion bucks in just three days — faster than any movie in history,” Schneider said. Based on preorder figures, “GTA VI” has already easily cleared that milestone. The production costs are another scale, too. Even the biggest Hollywood blockbusters typically cost a few hundred million dollars to make; estimates for “GTA VI” exceed $1 billion. Schneider pointed out that other video game publishers, and even movie studios, have “cleared out of the way,” choosing not to release many new titles starting Thursday because “everyone who is into video games will play ‘GTA VI’ and will have time for little else.” “With so many paid and free-to-play games vying for people’s attention, time — not money — is the most precious commodity for gamers,” he added. This moment is decades in the making. Stephen Totilo, who has covered the industry for 20 years and now publishes the video game newsletter Game File, pointed out that “GTA” has been a premier franchise for a quarter-century. “From 2001 through 2013, GTA’s developers at Rockstar Games released five big games in the series, plus a slew of spin-offs,” he said. But since then, “Rockstar has released no new GTA games at all.” Not since the first year of Barack Obama’s second term. So there’s a lot of pent-up demand. Rockstar could afford to take its time, though, because “GTA V” never stopped being a blockbuster. The game has sold nearly 235 million copies worldwide, according to Take-Two, and its online multiplayer mode has kept players coming back — and spending money — for more than a decade. An entire generation of gamers has grown up in the interim: Kids who were in kindergarten when “GTA V” came out are now in college. Rockstar, a subsidiary of Take-Two, targeted a 2025 launch date but repeatedly delayed it, further raising the stakes for this week. Retailers, broadband providers and fast-food chains have all tried to tap into the launch excitement with promotions and ad campaigns. It’s about more than stealing cars “It might be hard for some non-gamers to understand the appeal of ‘GTA,’” Totilo acknowledged. “They might even be unnerved by it, if they remember headlines from the early 2000s about the violence in the games.” “On one level, they’re just a more complex take on Pac-Man,” Totilo said. “At their core, they’re games about chasing and being chased, except there are no ghosts, fruits nor simple grids,” he said. “Instead, they play out in fictionalized versions of New York, Los Angeles or GTA VI’s Vice City riff on Miami, with the player in control of the crooks and the police in hot pursuit.” Rockstar “has added a love story this time,” he noted: “You play as both members of a criminal couple. Think of GTA VI as an interactive Bonnie and Clyde, where you control the dramatic, violent lives of two robbers in love.” Some of this gameplay was previewed in a first-of-its-kind trailer that Netflix streamed around the world in August. Totilo also emphasized the open-ended nature of the “GTA” franchise. “Rockstar creates meticulously detailed cities full of streets and alleys to explore, populates them with virtual citizens for players to meet, records scores of radio stations — some with music, but talk radio, too — to tune into. They fill the map with activities to try out, then set players loose.” And loose doesn’t always mean violent: Totilo said he spent part of a recent “GTA” night delivering virtual pizzas in his virtual city. Schneider said that for IGN, a decades-old video gaming website, “a new game from Rockstar means a sustained traffic spike for multiple years as people come to us for review coverage, guides, and game maps.” “We’ll all be awake at 3:00 am, publishing content, when GTA VI releases in New Zealand — the first place it’ll be available in the world,” he said. “We expect many gamers to change their console settings and spoof their place of residence just to play a few precious hours earlier.”

articles.title: Nvidia to report Q3 earnings amid Huang scandal
articles.summary: Nvidia will report its third quarter earnings after the bell Tuesday.
articles.body:
Nvidia will report its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, its first major public event since former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid an affairs scandal.

Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's CFO, will host the call, during which she'll likely address the matter, though she'll likely go into little detail.

According to the Financial Times , Huang is considering a comeback with backing from Silicon Valley executives. CNBC, however, reports that Nvidia's board is not looking to bring Huang back.

Potential names that could replace Huang include internal candidates such as Nvidia VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing Ian Buck and outsiders such as Arm CEO Rene Haas, who previously worked at Nvidia.

The embattled Huang resigned from Nvidia last week after revelations that he had alleged affairs with a woman acting as a Chinese spy and with a fellow executive at the company.

Nvidia's board has launched an investigation into the alleged spy affair, but says it has no reason to believe Nvidia or national security secrets were compromised.

Nvidia's stock price has taken a serious hit since the Huang scandal broke out, and is now down nearly 17% year to date.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Analysts across Wall Street have responded to the shake-up by lowering price targets on or downgrading Nvidia's stock. While the consensus is that the company is in good hands under Kress for the time being and that sales are already locked in for next year, there are also questions about the company's long-term outlook.

For the third quarter, Nvidia is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2.47 on revenue of $109.15 billion, up from $1.30 and $57 billion in Q3 last year.

Data Center revenue is projected to peak at $101.85 billion, with Hyperscale bringing in $53.61 billion and AI Clouds, Industrial, & Enterprise at $48.64 billion.

Nvidia's Edge Computing business, which includes everything from gaming chips to automotive technology, is expected to generate $7.49 billion in sales.
