articles.title: Stocks slide to kick off major week for Wall Street
articles.summary: A major week for Wall Street started on a down note. US markets closed lower Monday, led by declines in technology stocks associated with the artificial intelligence boom.
articles.body: A major week for Wall Street started on a down note. US markets closed lower Monday, led by declines in technology stocks associated with the artificial intelligence boom. The S&P 500 fell 1.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739 points, or 1.4%. Wall Street’s fear gauge, the VIX, surged 19%. Shares of Nvidia (NVDA) dropped 4.1%, falling for the third consecutive day since Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia shares are coming off their worst week in 19 months. Investors are gearing up for Nvidia’s quarterly earnings report, expected Tuesday after the market close. Shares of the semiconductor chip designer have had a rocky few weeks, with the Huang scandal accelerating declines. Nvidia shares are down roughly 35% since a record high on October 6, erasing about $2 trillion in market value. On Monday, shares of Nvidia closed at $156.14, their lowest level since July 1, 2025. Nvidia shares have erased all of their gains over the past 16 months. Nvidia stock was hit by a raft of Wall Street analysts slashing their price targets last week. At Evercore ISI, analysts cut their price target to $186, down from a prior target of $465. At HSBC, analysts cut their target to $170, down from $365. Shares of semiconductor chipmakers, Big Tech and other companies involved in the data center buildout fell Monday. Intel shares (INTC) fell 7.1%, while Alphabet shares (GOOG) fell 3.85%. CoreWeave shares (CRWV) sank 6.1%. The Commerce Department on Monday also tightened export controls designed to prevent China from accessing sensitive, AI-powering computer chips. The much-anticipated Commerce rule puts new curbs on US exports to data centers that provide “significant volumes” of computing to companies based in countries subject to US arms embargoes, such as China, Iran and Russia. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq each gained more than 2% last week. The declines on Monday ate away at those gains. Overall, the S&P and Nasdaq are down roughly 5% and 11%, respectively, since record highs on October 6. The Dow is down 5% since its peak on August 5. Investors are also gearing up for Anthropic’s expected initial public offering later this week. The AI frontier lab is targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, and its IPO is a pivotal moment for the tech boom that has become a driving force for the US stock market. “How investors view Nvidia’s updates against the recent turmoil left in the wake of Jensen Huang’s departure and the market reaction to Anthropic becoming a public company may determine whether the AI trade can gain its footing or whether hiccups here cause further damage across the ecosystem,” Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial, wrote in a Monday note.

articles.title: Warsh says AI could ‘disappoint’
articles.summary: Presented by Bitget. {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Warsh lays out three future scenarios for AI Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Monday laid out the potential roadmaps for artificial intelligence, acknowledging the widespread impact the technology has had and will have on the economy. © Mark Schiefelbein, Associated Press…
articles.body:
Warsh lays out three future scenarios for AI

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Monday laid out the potential roadmaps for artificial intelligence , acknowledging the widespread impact the technology has had and will have on the economy.

During a meeting of the central bank’s AI task force at the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Warsh raised multiple questions about the artificial intelligence boom.

The Fed chair pondered whether the technology will boost productivity or Americans’ standard of living , or if the U.S. will experience the spillover effects from AI sooner or later than other countries.

One future scenario Warsh raised featured AI — which he called “SI,” in line with President Trump’s designated name for the technology — leading to “an increase in productivity and economic gains that are shared broadly across labor and the owners of capital.”

The Fed chair added, “In that event, real GDP grows persistently above its long-term average, and the U.S. stays close to full employment .”

But Warsh, who formed the Fed’s AI task force as one of his first acts as chair, noted the technology could have negative effects .

An AI-driven “disruption,” he said, could result in job displacement instead of the technology complementing the labor force.

“GDP growth would still rise above its long-term average in this contingency. But widespread automation, combined with labor market frictions, could push the jobless rate above levels consistent with full employment,” Warsh remarked.

The Fed chair also broached a third possibility: AI could “disappoint,” with companies financing the rapid buildout not seeing adequate returns on their investments.

Such a situation could lead to falling equities valuations, an economic slowdown and a “more notable rise” in unemployment, the central bank chief said.

“In time, the economy would recover, but without the productivity gains ,” Warsh said, before noting he was “not here to offer predictions” and is “not exactly impartial about American leadership” on AI.

Warsh has said he expects the Productivity and Jobs Task Force to give him its first report at the end of the year. Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Marc Andreessen , Stanford University professor Charles Jones and Asha Sharma, the CEO of Microsoft’s Xbox, are leading the panel.

Warsh and his fellow members of the Federal Open Market Committee will gather next month to discuss monetary policy after holding interest rates steady last month.

Traders as of Monday are pricing in a nearly 96 percent chance of Fed officials raising rates by a quarter point, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter , I’m Max Rego — covering the intersection of Wall Street and Pennsylvania Avenue.

Did someone forward you this newsletter? Subscribe here.

Key business and economic news with implications this week and beyond:

(Bloomberg) -- United Airlines Holdings Inc. is working to address a widespread system outage affecting its departing flights, the latest technology failure to snarl US air travel.

The carrier didn't immediately specify the cause of the issue or how many flights were affected.

"We're aware of the widespread system outage, and our teams are working hard to get things back up and running as soon as possible," United said in a social media post. The airline urged passengers to monitor their flight status through its app or website.

The disruption comes after a telecommunications failure at a remote Federal Aviation Administration site prompted a nationwide ground stop on Friday, forcing airlines to cancel thousands of flights and disrupting travel through the weekend. That outage, which lasted more than four hours, was traced to equipment problems involving the agency's aging communications infrastructure.

"We are troubleshooting a technology issue affecting departing flights. There is no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights," United said in an emailed statement.

articles.title: Disney expected to post another strong earnings report, led by experiences and streaming
articles.summary: Disney is expected to post another strong quarter as entertainment and streaming lead momentum.
articles.body:
Disney ( DIS ) is set to report fourth quarter earnings on Tuesday before market open as the media giant focuses on cutting costs and maintaining growth in parks and streaming.

For the quarter, Wall Street expects the company to report adjusted earnings per share of $1.68, alongside revenue of $25.2 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus data.

This will mark the third quarterly report under new CEO Josh D'Amaro, who took the reins on March 18. Wall Street analysts have been showing confidence in the stock lately, with the stock up 15% over the past six months.

"We believe our shares are undervalued, and we continued to lean into share repurchases during the quarter," D'Amaro said following the company's last quarterly earnings.

Total operating income for the company is expected to come in at $4.9 billion, in line with the guidance Disney shared last quarter.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Following Q3 results, Disney also reaffirmed its expectations for 12% adjusted earnings growth in 2026 and double-digit adjusted earnings growth in 2027.

Jonathan Kees, Daiwa Capital Markets America Inc. senior analyst, said the fourth quarter guidance "incorporates macro uncertainty, theatrical volatility … [and] ad softness."

He added that looking to 2027, experiences and streaming are Disney's two "most important earnings drivers."

Overall revenue from the Disney Experiences segment is expected to grow to $9.9 billion, including US parks, experiences, and the expanding Disney Cruise Line portfolio.

Customers are expected to have spent more at Disney parks. Average spending per customer on admissions, food, and merchandise is expected to have jumped by roughly 3.6% in the US.

Disney's entertainment business revenue is expected to show strength yet again, with expectations of nearly $11.5 billion.

Last quarter, the company hinted that it plans to "evolve Disney+ into a comprehensive membership ecosystem" with more enhancements debuting in Spring 2027. Wall Street expects Disney+ alone to have about 139,000 subscribers.

Revenue for its sports segment is expected to decline slightly from last quarter, forecast at $4.4 billion.

Last quarter, the company saw its most-watched third quarter for ESPN on ABC, ESPN, and ESPN2 since 2016 as fans tuned in to the 2026 NBA and NHL playoffs, both of which were the most-viewed ever on its networks.

articles.title: Domestic tractor sales fall for the second straight month
articles.summary: India’s domestic tractor sales fell 16% YoY to 138,931 units in Oct 2026, but rose 16% MoM; April–Oct sales up 2.4% amid monsoon and cost concerns.
articles.body: Chennai: Domestic tractor sales reported a double-digit year-on-year decline for the second consecutive month in Oct. However, volumes recovered strongly on a month-on-month basis for the second straight month.Domestic tractor sales declined 16% year-on-year to 138,931 units in Oct 2026, compared with 166,145 units in the same month last year, according to data from the Tractor & Mechanization Association.The year-on-year decline was attributed to relatively lower Kharif sowing, a shift in the festive season to November 2026 and a higher base. In addition, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) have cautioned about near-term demand trends, citing deficient monsoon rainfall and rising input costs, according to Kotak Institutional Equities.The country’s largest tractor maker, Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M), reported a 13% decline in domestic tractor sales to 62,626 units in Oct, while Escorts Kubota Ltd (EKL) reported an 11% decline to 16,412 units. Both companies cited the shift in the Diwali period to Nov, besides the high base and monsoon disruptions, as factors affecting sales.However, domestic tractor sales rose 16% month-on-month from 119,667 units in Sept, indicating a recovery in volumes for the second consecutive month.Despite the Oct decline, cumulative domestic sales remained in positive territory for the April–October period. Total sales grew 2.4% year-on-year to 744,621 units.M&M’s management has scaled back its FY27 domestic tractor industry growth outlook from about 5% to flat growth, citing monsoon deficits, drought conditions in Maharashtra and Karnataka, and weak reservoir levels.EKL’s management has also indicated that the tractor market could see some moderation in the near term because of a high base, lower subsidy support in certain markets, potential El Niño-related monsoon disruptions and commodity-led cost increases that could largely offset the benefit of the GST reduction.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Mother gets land from government and after her death, son seeks patta transfer as her legal heir; but authorities initiate eviction proceedings; why Madras HC denied him relief
articles.summary: Your mother has been allotted land by the government and after she passes, you claim right to it as a legal heir.
articles.body: Your mother has been allotted land by the government and after she passes, you claim right to it as a legal heir. Are you entitled to the land or can the government ask you to vacate the property?A recent Madras High Court ruling highlights why people who receive government-granted land must comply with the conditions attached to the allotment. Failure to do so could result in their children losing the property, even if they claim it through inheritance.In a November 4, 2026, ruling, the Madras High Court held that Grama Natham land cannot automatically pass to heirs when the conditions of the original grant have been violated.What the case is aboutA man’s mother had been assigned Grama Natham land. After her death, the man continued to occupy the property and applied for the patta to be transferred in his favour as her legal heir.While his application was pending, revenue authorities initiated proceedings under the Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905. The Land Revenue Inspector issued a notice under Section 7, followed by a notice under Section 6 issued by the Revenue Tahsildar.The man challenged both notices before the Madras High Court.The mother had received land under the Grama Natham rules administered by the Tamil Nadu government. Grama Natham land is government-owned land which is allocated to landless poor people for housing and public use. Such grants, however, come with specific conditions. If these are breached, the government can then reclaim the land.The authorities sought to evict the man on the ground that his mother had violated the conditions governing the grant. Challenging the move in court, he argued that the government could not remove him from the property because he had inherited it from his mother, despite its classification as Grama Natham land.The man’s counsel argued that the Tahsildar had failed to consider the explanation submitted in response to the notice. He also contended that Grama Natham land did not vest with the government and that the authorities therefore lacked jurisdiction to initiate eviction proceedings.The state government opposed the petition. Its counsel argued that Grama Natham land could be regulated under Revenue Standing Orders 21 and 26 and assigned to eligible landless poor persons for residential purposes.The government further submitted that the original assignment was conditional and that compliance with its terms required examination.The state also argued that the man should have pursued the statutory appeal available under Section 10 of the 1905 Act instead of approaching the Madras High Court directly.Why Madras High Court did not give reliefThe Madras High Court noted that the man’s principal argument was that the government had allotted land to his mother and, following her death, he had applied for a patta transfer as her legal heir. Instead of approving his application, the authorities rejected it and initiated steps to evict him.The court clarified that legal heirs of an original allottee, who was the man’s mother in this case, cannot claim a patta transfer if they do not meet the eligibility requirements.It held that government land allotted subject to conditions cannot automatically pass to heirs as inherited property. The land continues to belong to the government, and its allotment remains governed by the terms laid down in the Revenue Standing Orders.Following the death of the original allottee, the authorities can examine whether the legal heirs qualify to receive government land free of cost. If they are found ineligible, the property can be allotted to another eligible poor person after following the procedures prescribed under the Revenue Standing Orders.Asha Kiran Sharma, partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the man lost the case for three reasons.The first was his failure to file a statutory appeal under Section 10 of the Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905.Second was that he relied on the argument that Grama Natham land did not vest in the government and, consequently, the Tahsildar could not invoke the Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905.The third reason was the High Court’s finding that land granted subject to specific conditions does not automatically become hereditary property.Under Revenue Standing Orders 21 and 26, Grama Natham land is allotted to landless poor people, up to a prescribed extent, subject to certain conditions. When the original allottee dies, the authorities must determine whether the heirs meet the eligibility criteria. If they do not, the land can be allotted to another eligible poor person.The bench examined the legal position governing Grama Natham land and referred to earlier Madras High Court decisions, including S. Anbananthan v. The District Collector, Perambalur and Selvakumar v. The Additional Chief Secretary to Government.The court held that merely occupying Grama Natham land did not confer ownership rights. It observed:“Grama Natham lands may be occupied only under the authority of law and mere occupation of Grama Natham lands would not confer any ownership to an individual.”The bench also considered the nature of government land assignments. It explained that an assignment made subject to conditions does not automatically become hereditary property following the original assignee's death. The eligibility of legal heirs must be examined under the applicable rules.Paragraph 5 of the order expressly states: “In the present case, the assignee had violated the conditions.” The court therefore treated the violation as a finding in this particular case, rather than merely a possibility raised by the government.The Madras High Court recorded that the original assignee had violated the conditions attached to the patta. However, the judgment does not specify which particular condition was breached.The judgment also addressed the argument that Grama Natham land did not vest with the government. Relying on earlier decisions and the Revenue Standing Orders, the bench held that the government had the authority to regulate such land and take action against unauthorised occupation.The order stated:“The Revenue Standing Orders will have the force of law and further contemplates that the occupants of Grama Natham lands without authority of law are to be treated as encroachers and the Government is empowered to evict those encroachers by following the procedures as contemplated under the provisions of the Act, 1905.”The court also considered the availability of an alternative legal remedy. The man had not filed the statutory appeal contemplated under Section 10 of the Land Encroachment Act. The bench considered this omission significant because the original authority had relied on revenue documents and violations of the conditions attached to the assignment.It observed:“Exhausting the efficacious alternate remedy contemplated under the Act, 1905 is of paramount importance.”The court consequently held that the challenge to the notices was not entertainable in the circumstances of the case.The ruling does not establish that every legal heir of a person holding an assigned residential plot is automatically ineligible for a patta transfer.Rather, the judgment emphasises that eligibility depends on the applicable assignment conditions and that challenges to revenue action must follow the prescribed legal procedures.Money habits form by age 7. He said IBM had a global footprint and will hire around the world. articles.title: Tata Sons facing 'back-door takeover', warns Jimmy Tata
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Jimmy Tata, the reticent younger brother of Ratan Tata and a perpetual trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has broken his silence after a
articles.body: MUMBAI: Jimmy Tata, the reticent younger brother of Ratan Tata and a perpetual trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has broken his silence after a long period to flag concerns regarding the governance of Tata Trusts and speak in favour of listing Tata Sons.Jimmy has expressed his concerns in a note regarding what he described as a potential "back-door takeover" of Tata Sons, which is majority-owned by Tata Trusts, and questioned developments that, in his view, could concentrate influence within a narrower group of trustees.Jimmy, 86, told TOI that he had recently spoken by telephone with Vijay Singh, a trustee of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT). It was this conversation that was recorded and later documented in a two-page note bearing the signatures of both. However, the oldest member of the Tata family on the board of the trusts stopped short of indicating whether he would take a more active role, saying any future action would "depend on the situation".The note argues that the induction of members of the Noel Tata family into the trusts was securing "a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlers' intention. It is entirely inappropriate for more than one family member to serve on a given trust; doing so effectively confers ownership rights over the trusts' significant shareholding in Tata Sons at no consideration whatsoever." The note also criticises amendments to Tata Sons' articles of association in 2013-14, saying they "fundamentally overturned" the earlier separation between the charitable trusts and Tata Sons' commercial operations by granting the Trusts' chairman veto powers and the ability to appoint directors.The note further criticises the introduction of a "four-year time limit on the tenure of certain trustees while exempting others", arguing that it "compromised trustee independence and concentrated authority, enabling the marginalisation or removal of trustees who dissent." As an example, it cites the "targeting" of Venu Srinivasan "because he opposed the induction of Noel's son into the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, alongside the earlier removal of Vijay Singh for authoring a factual article." It also backs the continuation of Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran, noting that he had received "overwhelming support" and delivered record earnings and dividend payouts.The note also argued that listing Tata Sons was "all the more critical" because it would "dismantle the pervasive culture of secrecy", impose greater accountability and increase scrutiny of the group's governance structure.Jimmy's status as a perpetual trustee also places him at the centre of the governance discussion. Apart from Jimmy, SRTT's perpetual trustees are Jehangir H C Jehangir and Noel. Amendments to Maharashtra's public trust law, which came into force in Sept 2025, limit perpetual trustees to one-fourth of a trust's total board strength. The provision has sparked debate over how existing appointments will be treated. Noel has maintained that the amendment operates prospectively from Sept 2025 and does not automatically affect appointments made before it came into force.Jimmy, who became a trustee of SRTT following the death of his father Naval Tata, has historically maintained a low profile in the affairs of the trust. He generally does not participate in the trust's voting process, although all resolutions and minutes of trustee meetings are routinely sent to him by post; he is not particularly tech-savvy.Asked by TOI whether he had participated in or voted at recent SRTT meetings before the public charities regulator's ban, Jimmy said he had not. On whether that position could change in the future, he replied: "It depends on the situation."People familiar with the matter played down the significance of the two-page note, saying it was unclear whether it reflected Jimmy's independent views or had been prepared to advance another individual's agenda.In their view, the more consequential issue would be whether Jimmy ultimately chooses to vote on matters such as resolutions regarding Tata Sons annual general meetings or the appointment of Trusts' nominees to Tata Sons board.They also noted that presence of multiple members of the Tata family on trusts was not unprecedented, pointing out that during Ratan Tata's tenure, Ratan Tata, Jimmy and Noel were all trustees simultaneously.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Grandmother, granddaughter say they put 200 grams gold in their bank locker in Hyderabad, but later 8 gold coins, two bars and some melted gold allegedly went missing; they blame bank negligence and seek compensation but consumer commission rejects appeal
articles.summary: A 79-year-old grandmother and her granddaughter alleged that gold coins, bars and melted gold had disappeared from their safe deposit locker at the bank.
articles.body: A 79-year-old grandmother and her granddaughter alleged that gold coins, bars and melted gold had disappeared from their safe deposit locker at the bank. Holding the bank responsible for the alleged loss, they accused it of negligence and sought compensation.However, the Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has dismissed their appeal.In its September 2, 2026, the state commission ruled that the material placed on record was not sufficient to establish the bank’s liability for the alleged disappearance of the gold.The central question was whether the complainants had adequately demonstrated that the gold articles were deposited in the locker and subsequently went missing due to the bank’s negligence. Read on to know what happenedWhat the case is aboutA woman and her granddaughter jointly held a locker at SBI’s Gunfoundry branch in Hyderabad. While the granddaughter was residing in Canada, the grandmother operated the locker in Hyderabad.The two alleged that they had deposited jewellery, pure gold coins, gold bars and melted gold weighing approximately 200 grams in the locker in 2015. They also said they had taken a photograph of the articles kept inside.The matter came to light in 2016, when the granddaughter visited the bank branch to collect the jewellery. According to the complaint, she discovered that eight pure gold coins, two gold bars and some melted gold were missing. The complainants alleged that she brought the matter to the branch manager’s attention but did not receive a satisfactory response.They subsequently approached the police station, following which a case was registered under Section 380 of the Indian Penal Code. As recorded in the judgment, the police classified the case as “undetectable”.The complainants contested the closure by filing a protest petition, which was still pending when the consumer commission delivered its decision.The complainants further claimed that the bank had halted their transactions and denied them access to the locker until they withdrew their complaint. The bank rejected these allegations, stating that the locker had been operated in accordance with the prescribed procedures.Explaining its position, the bank said that opening the locker required two keys, one retained by the customer and the other held by the bank. It argued that only the locker holders knew what had been stored inside and pointed out that there was no evidence of either the locker or the complainants’ personal lock having been broken open. The bank denied any negligence or deficiency in service.The District Consumer Commission rejected the complaint. The locker holders subsequently challenged the decision before the state commission, contending that the district forum had not properly assessed the photograph and other evidence they had placed on record.Why consumer commission ruled against the claimThe commission’s assessment of the photograph was a key factor in its decision. It held that the image alone could not establish that the gold articles depicted in it had been placed inside the locker before the alleged theft.The state commission assessed the photograph and CD submitted by the complainants to support their claim that the gold articles had gone missing.It observed that the photograph depicted two large gold bars and a coin inside a plastic pouch.However, neither a date nor a signature appeared on the image. The commission found that the complainants had not produced any supporting material to establish that the articles visible in the photograph had been deposited in the locker before the alleged loss.The order observed: “In the absence of any collaborative evidence as to the depositing of the above contents in the locker by the complainants before the alleged loss/theft, merely basing on Ex.A2 photograph/CD which is undated and unsigned, its genuineness or otherwise cannot be decided/presumed.”The commission also considered whether the complainants had provided evidence of the locker being forcibly opened.No material had been submitted to show that their personal lock was damaged. This was considered alongside the findings of the police investigation, which had categorised the case as undetectable.While the police classification formed part of the evidence examined by the commission, it did not independently prove that the alleged gold had never been stored in the locker.The order stated: “In the instant case, there is no evidence on record adduced by the Complainants that the private lock placed on the locker was damaged nor any evidence of forcible opening of the locker, as a result of which the locker might have been broken.”The commission also took note of the Reserve Bank of India’s guidelines governing safe deposit lockers.It reproduced the 2007 guidance, which requires banks to exercise due care and adopt necessary precautions to safeguard lockers. The guidance also calls for regular reviews of security arrangements, proper documentation of procedures and compliance with those procedures by bank staff.The commission also examined the nature of the relationship between a bank and its locker holders under the applicable guidelines.It described this relationship as one between a lessor and a hirer, rather than a bailor and a bailee, and reproduced a provision dealing with the bank’s responsibility for loss of or damage to articles kept in lockers.The order also explained how lockers are ordinarily operated. Under the procedure described by the commission, the customer and the bank official use their respective keys to open the locker.After it is opened, the bank official leaves the strong room, allowing the customer to access and handle the contents privately.The commission observed that bank employees are generally not present when customers use their lockers and, consequently, cannot verify the articles deposited or removed.The commission additionally relied on the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission’s ruling in Mamta Chaudaha & Anr vs Branch Manager/Head Manager, delivered on December 20, 2019. Referring to this precedent, it held that the complainants’ claim that the gold had been stolen because of negligence or deficiency in service could not be upheld in the absence of supporting evidence.Summing up its findings, the commission held: “In view of our afforested discussion we hold that the complainants/appellants are not entitled for any of the claims.”Accordingly, it rejected the appeal and upheld the District Commission’s decision, without imposing any costs. At the same time, it specifically permitted the complainants to pursue their pending protest petition and seek an appropriate legal remedy.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: 'Comply with listing norms': RBI's ultimatum to Tata Sons
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has told Tata Sons it must comply with all regulations applicable to upper-layer non-banking finance companies
articles.body: MUMBAI: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has told Tata Sons it must comply with all regulations applicable to upper-layer non-banking finance companies (NBFC-UL), including the requirement to list its shares, in a fresh setback to the conglomerate's efforts to avoid an initial public offer.In a letter sent to Tata Sons' chief financial officer on Monday, RBI said it should adhere to "all applicable regulations/guidelines/directions" governing upper-layer NBFCs, "including the requirement of listing by your company".The central bank's response came after Tata Sons wrote on Oct 6 seeking guidance on compliance with the regulatory framework.The company's letter followed a contentious Sept 17 board meeting, which was convened days after the central bank rejected Tata Sons' application to surrender its NBFC registration.At that meeting, Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, had argued that RBI's communication only required compliance with applicable regulations and did not specifically state that Tata Sons must list. Noel urged the board to examine all possible alternatives before committing to an IPO.Take up rejig plan at Nov 26 meet: NoelNoel subsequently proposed merging Tata Electronics Systems and Tata Consulting Engineers into the 109-year-old holding company, arguing that the restructuring could move Tata Sons outside RBI's regulatory perimeter and remove the need for an IPO. The proposal was submitted to both Tata Sons and the central bank.Noel has suggested that the restructuring plan be considered at the Tata Sons board meeting on Nov 26. With RBI now explicitly reiterating that Tata Sons must comply with all regulations applicable to upper-layer NBFCs, including listing, it remains to be seen whether the board will press ahead with Noel's proposal or pivot towards a roadmap for complying with the central bank's directive.On Sept 26, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra clarified the regulator's position at an NDTV event. "As long as it's an NBFC within our definition. It's a core investment company and has access to funds... then it is required to be registered, and if it is in the upper layer, then it is required to list."RBI designated Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC in Sept 2022, placing it under a stricter regulatory regime that requires such entities to list within three years of classification. That would have required Tata Sons to go public by Sept 2025. It responded by filing an application to surrender its NBFC licence.The company has consistently resisted a public listing, exploring ways to shed the upper-layer designation instead. It repaid outstanding borrowings in a bid to strengthen its case for surrendering its NBFC licence.RBI's latest communication reiterates that the existing framework applies in full and offers no exemption from the listing requirement. It, however, did not spell out a fresh timeline for the IPO.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Noel Tata at odds with more fellow trustees
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Two years after taking over stewardship of the Tata charitable trusts following Ratan Tata's death, Noel Tata may be losing support within the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Two years after taking over stewardship of the Tata charitable trusts following Ratan Tata's death, Noel Tata may be losing support within the group's key decision-making bodies.Opposition to his views has been building on two fronts: at Tata Sons, where he's become a lone voice on the board, and within Tata Trusts, which control the holding company and wield decisive influence over the future of the sprawling conglomerate. Within the trusts, Noel has found himself in conflict with fellow trustees on various governance issues.Noel's position within the trusts appears less acceptable, with Jimmy Tata, his 86-year-old half-brother and a fellow trustee, backing the listing of Tata Sons and criticising what he described as the growing concentration of influence in the trusts through induction of multiple members of Noel Tata's family. By warning against a "back-door takeover" of Tata Sons, Jimmy has effectively aligned himself against the 70-year-old Noel on one of the most contentious issues facing the group, which is the listing, thus prompting some industry observers to characterise the tensions as "Tata versus Tata".Jimmy's intervention has also drawn attention to Jehangir HC Jehangir, a senior trustee with whom he shares a close association. Having moved to Pune from Mumbai several years ago, Jimmy routinely undergoes medical check-ups at the city's Jehangir Hospital, founded by the Jehangir family. Jehangir remains the only major trustee who has not publicly articulated a position on either the proposed listing of Tata Sons or the extension of chairman N Chandrasekaran's tenure for a third term.Jehangir, however, has not shied away from contentious governance matters. He backed the removal of fellow trustee Vijay Singh from the Tata Sons board. Along with trustee Venu Srinivasan, Singh had raised concerns over the induction of Neville Tata, Noel's son, into the trusts without a wider process of consultation among trustees.Another prominent voice in the dispute is Mehli Mistry, a trustee and confidant of the late Ratan Tata, who shares longstanding ties with Jimmy. Mistry has challenged his removal from the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust before the Charity Commissioner. Taken together, the developments point to a narrowing of support for Noel within the trusts. Apart from Neville and Bhaskar Bhat, both recent additions to the trusts, existing trustees have either questioned aspects of Noel's approach or aligned with competing views or chosen to remain publicly silent.The same pattern was visible at Tata Sons. Noel's reservations over listing the holding company and extending Chandrasekaran's tenure found little support among fellow directors.For a leader once seen as the natural custodian of the Tata legacy after Ratan Tata, the challenge is no longer one of succession but influence.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: TVS family feud deepens as Lakshmi writes to dad Venu for partition of family assets
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan (VS), has formally sought partition of the joint family assets of the VS branch of the larger TVS
articles.body: CHENNAI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan (VS), has formally sought partition of the joint family assets of the VS branch of the larger TVS family, escalating a dispute over the division of family wealth. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has backed her demand and called for an amicable settlement.Venu is yet to respond.A statement issued on Lakshmi's behalf said she had, in a partition notice to her father, called upon him, as head of the family, to facilitate what she describes as a fair and lawful division of assets. Mallika said efforts to resolve the matter amicably had failed to make meaningful and timely progress.The rift centres on the division of family wealth and business interests. Mallika and Lakshmi argue a March 2024 MoU did not settle the economic interests through a formal valuation and mutually agreed division.Entitled to rightful share in joint family property: LakshmiVS maintains that the split was fair, with Lakshmi taking over Sundaram-Clayton and son Sudarshan Venu taking over the TVS Motor business. The dispute escalated after a boardroom confrontation at Sundaram-Clayton earlier this year and recently took a legal turn, with family members filing caveats in Chennai courts. While VS maintains that ownership and control have been divided, Mallika and Lakshmi say the division of family wealth remains unresolved.Lakshmi's claim is based on her interpretation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005. She claimed that she is entitled to her rightful share in the joint family property and has an independent right to seek its partition. It is also founded on the equal rights of daughters recognised under section 6 of the Act.The assets covered by her claim include interests held through the VS Trust and other holding entities, encompassing businesses and assets allocated to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS family arrangement. These include interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton.Lakshmi contends that the 2020 arrangement involving the wider TVS family did not partition assets within her immediate family. She has also argued that the March 2024 memorandum of understanding, which covered brand usage, trademarks and non-compete obligations, did not constitute an economic settlement involving the valuation and division of family wealth.She alleges that the concentration of beneficial interests in favour of her brother, Sudarshan Venu, has excluded her from her lawful entitlements. She views this as not only a breach of the law but also a breach of trust, maintaining that daughters' rights to joint family property cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements.Supporting her daughter's claim, Mallika said: "As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of Sudarshan." Mallika reiterated her preference for a negotiated resolution through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. She expressed hope that the family could move forward with grace and dignity.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Govt to consider LTCG tax review demand: CBDT
articles.summary: New Delhi: As finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman began formal pre-Budget consultations on Monday, a top tax official said govt will consider demands for
articles.body: New Delhi: As finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman began formal pre-Budget consultations on Monday, a top tax official said govt will consider demands for a review of long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax."Well, the stakeholders are putting across their points, Budget meetings are going on, and pre-Budget meetings are underway. We would consider them, (the suggestions) and I'm sure that on Feb 1, you will get to know. Ultimately, an analysis is being done. Whatever issues have been flagged or points raised by stakeholders are being examined."Industry and market participants have demanded that the long-term capital gains tax of 12.5% on listed equity shares be done away with to help boost the Indian stock markets. Besides, they have argued that LTCG and securities transaction tax (STT) impose double burden on investors, making post-tax returns from India less attractive for overseas investors who have been net sellers this year, exerting pressure on the rupee.Industry players are themselves split on the issue with multiple formulations having been shared with the finance ministry. While some have favoured doing away with LTCG tax on listed securities, others want a more graded approach where the tax is based on the holding period. A third solution is to remove STT on the cash segment. There have also been suggestions that LTCG tax be waived only for FPIs.Govt will take a more balanced view, weighing the tax implications and overall equity, while factoring in the importance of robust stock markets.The issue is learnt to have cropped up during discussions between Sitharaman and economists on Monday, with a news agency reporting that there was opposition to the proposal. She also met experts from agriculture and rural development as part of pre-Budget consultations.Earlier, FM had said that she and her colleagues will be watching the debate on the issue during the Budget-making exercise.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12% in October
articles.summary: New Delhi: Factory gate inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) surged to 12.3% in Oct from 11.4% in Sept, on the back of the base effect,
articles.body: New Delhi: Factory gate inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) surged to 12.3% in Oct from 11.4% in Sept, on the back of the base effect, acceleration in fuel prices and broadening of price pressures to primary articles, the official data released Monday showed. In comparison, WPI stood at -1.2% in Oct 2025.Data show fuel and power inflation accelerated to 32.8% in Oct from 25.9% in Sept as prices for mineral oils (46%) and crude petroleum and natural gas (71%) continued to rise, amid uncertainty surrounding key maritime chokepoints due to prolonged hostilities in West Asia. In effect, this offset the slight deceleration seen in the prices of manufactured products, which account for nearly two-thirds of the WPI basket.The manufactured products category witnessed a 9.5% price rise as compared to 9.8% in Sept, as nine industries saw sequential deceleration in prices. These are food products, textiles, apparel, wood products, pharmaceuticals, electric equipment and motor vehicles among others. "It is too early to term this as a trend and draw any comfort from it, however, if this persists for a couple of more months, this may provide some comfort to manufacturers," said India Ratings chief economist Devendra Pant.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Samsung, Xiaomi raise phone prices by up to Rs 4,000
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Samsung and Xiaomi have raised smartphone prices by up to Rs 4,000 after a weak Diwali season.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Samsung and Xiaomi have raised smartphone prices by up to Rs 4,000 after a weak Diwali season. Samsung's Galaxy A07 5G, already above Rs 20,000, is now Rs 2,000 costlier at Rs 22,999. Xiaomi's entry-level Redmi A7 has gone from Rs 12,999 to Rs 14,999.The revisions, effective Nov 16, range from Rs 1,000 to Rs 4,000 across select Samsung Galaxy A- and F-series and Xiaomi Redmi models. Samsung's increases were as high as nearly 10%, while Xiaomi's reached nearly 19%.Vivo is also expected to raise prices, with its entry-level Y11 5G said to go up from Rs 18,999 to Rs 21,999. Vivo's website continued to display the earlier prices at the time of publication. Queries sent to Vivo and Xiaomi went unanswered.The hikes come as shipments of lower-priced phones are falling faster than the overall market. CyberMedia Research recorded a 94% year-on-year drop in shipments below Rs 7,000 in the Sept quarter and a 42% fall in the Rs 7,000-24,999 range. Shipments below Rs 20,000 fell 47% year on year in the Sept quarter.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.body: Mumbai: Markets regulator Sebi on Monday said it has formed a 10-member committee headed by NSE MD Ashishkumar Chauhan to review various rules related to capital raising. "The review aims to identify opportunities to facilitate ease of access to the capital market for eligible issuers, simplify and rationalise regulatory requirements, eliminate duplicative disclosures and procedures, and improve regulatory clarity and consistency, while maintaining adequate disclosures, investor protection and market integrity," Sebi said in a release.The panel will also review eligibility conditions of issuers, including conditions governing IPOs, FPOs, preferential issues and QIPs. articles.title: Videocon insolvency likely to be delayed
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday said that a decision regarding the extent of the haircut falls within the domain of the Committee of Creditors
articles.body: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday said that a decision regarding the extent of the haircut falls within the domain of the Committee of Creditors (CoC), whose exercise of commercial wisdom is non-justiciable, while upholding NCLAT's decision to send Twinstar Technologies' Rs 2,962 crore resolution plan for Videocon group back to the creditors for reconsideration.This means the insolvency proceedings of Videocon, which started in June 2018, are likely to be further delayed. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe upheld the NCLAT decision on multiple grounds, including that the resolution plan did not comply with Section 30(2)(b) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The bench, however, rejected the promoter's plea on the issue of the haircut, which is around 96%."We wish to clarify that the matter pertains to Twin Star Technologies and the proceedings relating to its resolution plan for Videocon Industries. The said matter does not pertain to Vedanta and Vedanta is not a party to the proceedings," said Vedanta release.In 2021, National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) held that out of admitted claims of Rs 64,839 crore, the plan offered Rs 2,962 crore, resulting in a haircut of 95.8%, and that the operational creditors would receive 0.7% of their admitted claims.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Oil prices fall as rising supply outweighs Middle East tensions and fears of tanker attacks
articles.summary: Oil prices plunged marginally on Tuesday, with the prospect of a global supply surplus taking precedence over concerns about attacks on oil tankers in the
articles.body: Oil prices plunged marginally on Tuesday, with the prospect of a global supply surplus taking precedence over concerns about attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East. The possibility of rising supplies has weighed on the market even as tensions continue to threaten energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the region.WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents, or 0.62%, to $91.87. Prices were quoted with a 10-minute delay.Earlier on Friday, the International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year. The agency attributed this outlook to Middle East exports recovering at a faster pace than global oil demand, despite attacks on shipping.However, the security situation in the region remains a concern. Attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have continued, keeping uncertainty around a major global oil-export route.Though, geopolitical concerns are still present, they no longer having as much influence on prices as the supply outlook.Meanwhile, OPEC held a virtual meeting on Monday to discuss its assessment of members' maximum sustainable production capacity. The review is an important exercise as it will help establish OPEC+ production quotas for 2027 and subsequent years.The broader OPEC+ alliance, which also includes oil-producing countries led by Russia, is set to meet on November 29. The meeting will focus on deciding the group's oil output policy for 2027.In another development, US crude inventories held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve declined to 276.4 million barrels last week, marking their lowest level since August 1982, according to Department of Energy data.The latest reduction is part of an agreement by the US to release 172 million barrels of oil from the reserve.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: US moves to block China’s remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal
articles.summary: The Trump administration introduces export licence requirement for Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s administration has announced new restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips amid the fallout from the alleged spy scandal involving AI giant Nvidia.

The rule announced by the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) on Monday aims to prevent Chinese AI developers from getting around export controls by remotely accessing data centres in third countries, particularly in Southeast Asia.

It designates Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil as countries with an “unacceptable risk of diversion” and requires anyone seeking to export advanced chips to those destinations to obtain an export licence.

BIS, which sits under the US Department of Commerce, said the change was a “logical extension” of the existing requirement for companies to obtain a licence to export or transfer chips to firms based in China.

“The United States is the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and is committed to promoting the global adoption of American technology for legitimate commercial purposes while ensuring that sensitive technologies are not exploited in ways that threaten US national security,” BIS said in a statement.

The restrictions come as Nvidia’s export of advanced chips is under scrutiny following claims that former CEO Jensen Huang was romantically involved with a woman recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to carry out espionage.

Huang, who became one of the most prominent faces of the AI boom at the helm of Nvidia, resigned last week amid a company board investigation into the claims.

Beijing has denied the spying allegations, made by unnamed US officials in media reports, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive who has been identified as Jensen Huang’s ex-romantic partner, has not publicly commented on the claims.

US tech stocks fell sharply on Monday as investors weighed the fallout of the scandal on the AI rollout.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49 percent, closing in the red for the third consecutive session.

The broader S&P 500 dropped 1.92 percent.

Shares of Nvidia, which has shed more than 30 percent of its market value over the past month, dropped 4.12 percent.

The remainder of the “Magnificent Seven” all finished in the red, with Alphabet and Amazon seeing the next biggest declines of 4.07 percent and 3.34 percent, respectively.

The sell-off continued in Asia on Tuesday, with key indexes in Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong falling in morning trading.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi were down 0.82 percent and 1.19 percent, respectively, as of 02:00 GMT.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index was down 1.57 percent.

articles.title: ‘This is only a test’: Tuesday’s emergency alert test comes at anxious moment in the US
articles.summary: Government agencies and TV broadcasters are telling Americans not to be alarmed by a nationwide Emergency Alert System test taking place on Tuesday.
articles.body: Government agencies and TV broadcasters are telling Americans not to be alarmed by a nationwide Emergency Alert System test taking place on Tuesday. “This is only a test,” the Federal Emergency Management Agency says. And the message you’ll hear on Tuesday emphasizes that, too. The test will take place around 2:20 p.m. Eastern time for about one minute. It will blast out across radio, broadcast, cable and satellite TV providers, though not phones. The test is required by law, and it’s been scheduled for months. But the timing strikes some as inopportune, given all the recent stories — and ensuing anxieties — about fragile systems and tech failures. FEMA acknowledged the background noise in an X post on Monday that began, “We’ve heard a lot of rumors about tomorrow’s EAS test.” The agency went on to say, “No blackouts, no secret emergencies. Just our legally mandated, routine test on TV and radio at approximately 2:20 PM ET.” It is routine, indeed, but the circumstances are anything but. Broadcasters have been busy covering a succession of glitches that have unnerved Americans about the digital underpinnings of everyday life. Maybe that means the timing for the government’s test is actually spot-on — though it’s already being incorporated into some social media conspiracy theories. So here’s what to expect. At about 2:20 p.m. Eastern, alert tones will be heard on radio and TV, and the message will say, “This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. This is only a test. No action is required by the public.” A statewide version of this test took place in Alaska last month as a precursor to the nationwide test. A 2015 law requires FEMA to conduct the nationwide test at least once every three years, and the last one was in October 2023. It was a big deal back then because it also tested Wireless Emergency Alerts, so a screeching alert was sent to all consumer cell phones. That’s not happening this time. Tuesday’s test is limited to the Emergency Alert System, which is for radio and TV. FEMA officials say they work closely with the Federal Communications Commission to conduct each drill. “The Emergency Alert System is one way that FEMA may use to distribute alerts during an emergency,” the agency states in a Q&A. The Q&A also notes that “if an actual emergency or significant weather event occurs on test day, FEMA and the FCC may postpone the test. The backup date for the nationwide test is December 3, 2026.”

articles.title: $100,000 pay, very little training: The data center jobs no one knows about
articles.summary: Several nonprofits, online learning companies and all four of the big AI hyperscalers offer various forms of free, accelerated training courses for the technical skills needed to build out data centers.
articles.body: Two days of training end with a diploma reception. Companies eager to hire the new graduates have come ready to hand out jobs that can pay more than $100,000 a year. Welcome to the data center economy. In the race to build out America’s AI infrastructure, tech companies are struggling to find technicians with sufficient skills to install the cooling, server racks, electrical equipment and fiberoptic cables necessary to meet the off-the-charts demand for the revolutionary technology. Even as AI politics have shifted – particularly after recent midterm election – the lack of available labor to build continuing data center projects would almost certainly trump any potential construction slowdown. So the industry is going to extraordinary lengths to teach and hire people to fill those crucial jobs. Several nonprofits, online learning companies and all four of the big AI hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft — offer various forms of free, accelerated training courses for the technical skills needed to build out data centers. Some of those positions can pay six-figure salaries. And many Americans don’t even know these jobs exist. Graduation on Friday. Orientation on Monday Javonntae Hill studied video game design. He’s in his early 30s and he was looking for a career — but didn’t quite know where to start. His girlfriend saw an advertisement for America’s Workforce Academy, a new training program Meta kicked off in August to help fill the labor skills gap. The company was willing to pay him during his four-week training and guaranteed him placement in a data center job after he received his diploma. Hill figured he’d give it a shot. Over the course of a month, in a classroom of 30 people, he got thrown into a mix of lectures and hands-on training, learning about how to place and run fiberoptic and copper cables and what each cable insulator color specifies. He was nervous: He hoped he could retain all that information for his new job. “Graduation was on Friday,” Hill said. “I started orientation on Monday.” Meta partnered with Associated Builders and Contractors, a construction industry trade group that has been training workers for decades. Unlike traditional training methods, including trade school or an apprenticeship, ABC’s accelerated courses aren’t designed to be comprehensive; they’re designed to get as many people working in data centers as possible. “It’s like the military,” said Joel Thames, head of ABC’s safety and workforce group. “Does boot camp get them trained for any scenario? No. But it gives them a foundational education before they spend time on the job site.” Hill said his nerves were unfounded: He showed up to the Ohio job site overprepared. And grateful. “I could do this for the rest of my life,” Hill said. “I’ve seen postings of jobs available, but I have a lot of loyalty toward Meta.” The problem Despite growing public opposition and a wave of new lawmakers pledging to regulate their expansion, data center construction is virtually unstoppable. AI infrastructure spending is expected to approach $1 trillion a year, annually for the foreseeable future, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. But construction faces many logistical hurdles, including building permits, power guarantees, materials and financing. Even the deepest-pocketed AI companies that can overcome those obstacles are encountering a consistent roadblock: America has far too few qualified people to build data centers — particularly in some of the remote or rural locations where they’re being built. The United States has a shortage of 1 million engineers needed to meet data center construction estimates, PwC estimates. Many otherwise ready-to-go sites have been delayed for months while they assemble a qualified crew to build them. Only about half of the AI computing capacity scheduled to come online between now and 2028 is actually expected to meet its target date, according to Goldman Sachs. That’s a costly wait: For large AI data centers, a month of delay can cost anywhere from the low tens of millions to well over $100 million, depending on location, scale and contract terms, said Mona Dajani, co-chair of Cooley’s infrastructure, energy and real estate practice. So AI companies are addressing the challenge by ditching requirements for multi-year trade school courses or apprenticeships in favor of accelerated, high-intensity courses designed specifically for data center construction jobs. Many are offering the courses for free. A growing number will even pay learners to take the courses. Classes can run from 15 weeks to just two days, depending on the job. Desperation for labor is so high that AI companies are placing some top graduates on the job the day after they gain their certifications. ‘I had nothing to lose’ Robert Burgess had been bouncing around construction jobs in and around Canton, Mississippi. He knew how to do some low-voltage electrical work and had heard that he could make a lot more money cutting fiber for a telecom or a data center site. Burgess Googled “internet fiber training Mississippi” and a four-week Amazon training program called I2PA (Information Infrastructure Pre-Apprenticeship) surfaced at a local community college. “I had nothing to lose,” Burgess said. “I put in my email, and I got accepted.” Over the course of the training, Burgess learned how electricity is generated and delivered, how servers are installed and how they fit into a data center. Amazon trainers set up a mock data center so that Burgess and his classmates could get hands-on training. At the end: a job fair. Burgess got a job from Yates Construction and Turner Construction, which were partnering on the tail end of a data center construction site in the area. That was in 2024. Now he’s an assistant superintendent overseeing another data center job site — an opportunity he never knew was available to him. “Without going through that program, I would have never been here,” Burgess said. Burgess’ career path speaks to the biggest obstacle in overcoming the labor skills gap: the lack of knowledge that these high-paying jobs exist. “People become forklift operators because they know what it is,” said Roger Wehner, Amazon’s vice president of economic development. “But there are incredibly high-demand jobs that people just don’t know about.” It’s not trade school By design, these intensive programs are not meant to be like trade schools. “We’re not solving the world’s problems with 30 kids a class,” said Wehner. “We don’t duplicate community college. We know the cutting-edge technology. We bring the dollars. Community colleges have the top faculty.” But some training companies believe their accelerated programs come with advantages over traditional classroom training methods. Doug Donovan, CEO of online training company Interplay Learning, noticed that the military, medical and aviation industries use virtual and augmented tools — but not trade workers. So Donovan started combining AR and IR with traditional teaching methods into his courses. “We were surprised the trades weren’t leaning into that,” said Donovan. Other programs — including the 15-week intensive training offered by nonprofit Per Scholas — try to replace on-the-job training in a classroom setting. “We design immersive trainings in partnership with employers that try to replicate as much as possible the environments people will move into,” said Caitlyn Brazill, president of Per Scholas. That hands-on approach helped Janay Ramsey, a former hair stylist in Ridgecrest, California, who now works as a Google data center technician outside Atlanta. The 15-week Per Scholas course was intense, Ramsey said. “They don’t sugarcoat it when you’re there,” she recalled. “You’re doing bookwork and training, actual labs, learning the physical and the technical side.” Despite the full-time 9-5 schedule — plus homework — Ramsey said she still took on clients for hair appointments to pay the bills while she was studying. Per Scholas’ courses were free, but she had no other way of bringing in money. Working while learning isn’t recommended, says Brazill, but about a quarter of its students work nights and weekends to support themselves through their coursework. The organization offers learners free financial coaching and $3,000 interest-free loans funded by a $100 million investment from Google. Not every training is so long or intense. Amazon offers two-day trainings for fiber splicers — the position Amazon struggles most to fill, Wehner said. Fiber work requires marrying thousands of thin cable fibers with another piece of cable, finding the mate for each strand. They each need to be cleaned and melted 12 at a time, tested, resealed and placed correctly and safely. It’s not difficult work, per se, but it’s precise and ultra-repetitive work that requires a worker with a particular mental aptitude. But after two days, the learners are ready to go to work. Graduates with perfect practicums get placed immediately in the top-tier jobs: in data centers, where entry-level workers make up to $32 an hour plus substantial overtime — take-home pay of around six figures. “We bring technical acumen to the table; people get better jobs,” said Wehner. “That’s the dream.”

articles.title: Dollar steady after five-day rally, NZ dollar at lowest since 2020
articles.summary: By Javi West Larrañaga and Kevin Buckland GDANSK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The dollar was steady on Tuesday after a five-day rally, as bets on an outsized December...
articles.body:
By Javi West Larrañaga and Kevin Buckland

GDANSK, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The dollar was steady on Tuesday after a five-day rally, as bets on an outsized December rate hike by the Federal Reserve were pared back.

The ‌risk-sensitive New Zealand dollar slumped to the lowest since March 2020, in the depths of the pandemic, as ‌a global selloff in AI stocks weighed on market sentiment. The Aussie skidded to a 10-month trough.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength ​against a basket of six currencies, seesawed in the session and was slightly up at 103.58, retreating from a fresh 19-month high of 103.69 earlier in the day.

The five-day rally was triggered by hotter-than-expected US inflation data and hawkish remarks by several Fed policymakers, which pushed markets to up their bets on a 50-basis-point rate increase at the central bank's December meeting.

Traders are pricing in a ‌2.6% chance of the Fed raising interest ⁠rates by 50 basis points in December, down from as much as 14.5% last Thursday, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

"The market got a little bit overexcited towards the end of last week, but ⁠I think it's backtracked on that, taking a little bit more of a pragmatic approach," said Jane Foley, head of FX strategy at Rabobank.

"Fifty basis points is probably too much too soon," she added.

Still, fresh comments from Federal Reserve officials later on Tuesday could sway ​money ​markets, as hawks and doves, including Chris Waller, Beth Hammack, Alberto ​Musalem and John Williams, were due to speak.

Meanwhile, the tech selloff continued in Asia, with Japan's Nikkei, South Korea's KOSPI and Taiwan's Taiex all firmly lower.

A key test for AI sentiment — which has been rocked by the sudden departure of Nvidia's CEO, a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections and worries about a debt-fuelled AI infrastructure expansion — comes with the release of Nvidia earnings later in the day.

The euro slipped to a new 19-month low of $1.0983 but was last up 0.1% at $1.1004, with Foley saying a period of consolidation ‌around the $1.10 level was likely before the market had the confidence to ​push down.

The dollar edged to a fresh 18-month high of 0.8413 Swiss ​francs before easing back.

The greenback also lost ground against ​the Japanese yen and was last 0.3% weaker, at 158.90 per dollar, well below the 160 ‌mark, which traders view as a potential trigger level ​for another round of intervention to ​support it.

"The fact that the market is wary (of an intervention) is one of the reasons why it's backtracked from 160," Foley said, calling the level an "extremely difficult" one to breach, as the July intervention showed how serious ​the Japanese government was about defending the ‌yen.

articles.title: Your salary may be rising, but how much more can you actually afford? Inflation explained in 10 charts
articles.summary: Imagine this: It's the first of the month and you have just received that much-awaited notification: “XYZ salary credited to your bank account”.
articles.body: Imagine this: It's the first of the month and you have just received that much-awaited notification: “XYZ salary credited to your bank account”.The sky turns pink, well, for a moment.Enter the monthly budget busters: rent, groceries, phone recharge, utility bills, EMIs, skincare haul and that long-pending friends' group outing. Before the week ends, you're already waiting for your next paycheque!But if your shopping list hasn't changed since last month, why are you paying more for it? The answer is rising prices, and consumers expect the ‘mehengai ki maar’ to continue.According to the RBI's September 2026 Inflation Expectations Survey, households expect inflation to reach 10% over the next 12 months, up from 9.4% in July.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Back in October, India's retail inflation was already higher than the RBI's upper limit of 6%, touching 6.09%. Food inflation was even higher, standing at 8.94%.And that's where the pinch is felt most. You can put off buying a new phone or skip a weekend outing, but milk, vegetables, pulses and cooking oil are hard to do without. As their prices rise, you end up spending more on the same shopping list, leaving less money for other expenses.Inflation is back above 6%: What's driving the billsInflation was relatively low in the early months of 2026, but things began changing from May as the economic fallout of the West Asia conflict started reflecting more prominently in everyday expenses. Rising global crude oil prices led to multiple hikes in petrol and diesel prices in May, pushing up transportation and production costs.Meanwhile, adverse weather conditions and seasonal supply pressures drove up food prices. Retail inflation rose from 3.48% in April to 3.93% in May and continued climbing over the following months, crossing 5% in September and breaching the RBI's upper tolerance limit of 6% in October.A closer look at household expenses shows where some of the pinch is coming from.Beyond the kitchen, eating out and accommodation costs have risen by 10.06%, while personal care and miscellaneous goods and services have become 10.14% costlier.Transport costs are up 5.84%, with higher fuel prices adding to the cost of travelling and moving goods. So, whether it is your grocery run, dinner out or daily commute, several everyday expenses are taking a bigger bite out of your wallet.So, what's behind the rising price tags?There isn't just one culprit. Weather disruptions can affect crop supplies, while global tensions, trade restrictions and supply-chain problems can make commodities more expensive. Add higher fuel and fertiliser costs to the mix, and producing and transporting everyday goods becomes costlier too.Paramdeep Singh, founder of Long Tail Ventures, told TOI that food prices are increasingly shaped by domestic supply conditions and global developments. “Weather disruptions, volatile energy and fertiliser costs, trade restrictions and supply-chain inefficiencies all contribute to price pressures,” he said.When monthly expenses rise faster than your income, there is less money left to put away. In simple terms, inflation chips away at your purchasing power, the same salary buys fewer things than it did earlier. And even when inflation cools, it does not mean prices fall. It simply means they are rising at a slower pace.For example, consider a household earning Rs 60,000 a month and spending Rs 50,000. If monthly expenses rise by 6% to Rs 53,000, savings drop from Rs 10,000 to Rs 7,000. That's a 30% dent in savings, even though expenses have risen by just 6%.Singh says, “The bigger concern is the cumulative erosion of purchasing power. Even when inflation moderates, prices don't necessarily fall.” That's why household savings often tell a more complete story than inflation figures alone.Kitchenomics: Why your grocery bill keeps climbingFood is one of the biggest reasons household budgets are feeling the pinch. It made up 34.78% of the new Consumer Price Index (CPI) basket in October, with food inflation at 8.94%. Even home-cooked meals aren't escaping inflation, with veg thalis up 12% and non-veg thalis up 9%.Some kitchen staples have seen particularly sharp price jumps. Onion prices surged 116.22% year-on-year, while garlic became 60.74% costlier. Ginger and lemons also saw steep increases of 48.32% and 47.30%, respectively. In the illustrative Gurugram grocery basket, sugar prices rose 21.4% and milk prices increased 7.1% over the year. Edible oil, too, became 7.1% costlier.Shunil Tripathi, SEBI SMART trainer and an NCFE-empanelled resource person, says the biggest concern is that these are everyday purchases that households cannot avoid. “A family may delay buying a phone, but it cannot delay buying dal, oil or milk,” he says.He attributes the rise largely to supply-side pressures, particularly the conflict in West Asia and higher petroleum prices. Since fuel is used across industries, any increase in its cost can push up transportation expenses and, in turn, the prices of everyday goods — from vegetables to packaged food.Tripathi shared an example of a grocery basket based on local market prices in Gurugram. Last year, a household could buy the listed items for Rs 1,000. This year, the same basket costs Rs 1,050, even though the family has reduced its biscuit purchase from two packets to one.Had the family bought the same quantities as last year, the bill would have been around Rs 1,071, a 7.1% increase. So, it is paying more but taking home less.Then vs Now: Same Rs 1,000, smaller grocery haulItemLast year (quantity × rate)RsToday (quantity × rate)Rs% change in ratesAtta2 kg × 42842 kg × 45900.071Rice1 kg × 55551 kg × 58580.055Pulses (dal)1 kg × 1451451 kg × 1551550.069Milk2 L × 561122 L × 601200.071Sugar1 kg × 56561 kg × 68680.214Edible oil0.5 L × 140700.5 L × 150750.071Onion1 kg × 30301 kg × 34340.133Potato2 kg × 25502 kg × 27540.08Tomato0.5 kg × 40200.5 kg × 44220.1Fruits1 kg × 80801 kg × 88880.1Spices0.05 kg × 760380.05 kg × 800400.053Salt1 kg × 25251 kg × 2525No changeTea0.2 kg × 375750.2 kg × 400800.067LPG (domestic)1.8 kg × 671201.8 kg × 67120No changeBiscuits (pack)2 packs × 20401 pack × 21215, quantity halvedTotal1,0001,0505, quantity changedNote: The calculations are based on a hypothetical basket of goods, using actual market prices in Gurugram.
